courses.assessment_style: Single-best-answer MCQ (a-d), scenario-led, Nigerian and global organisation contexts

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Amid efforts to expand financial inclusion services across rural Nigeria, executives at United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA) introduced mobile invoice generation and instant loan processing for small businesses. Which principles are MOST clearly demonstrated?

options.a: Risk mitigation and performance benchmarking through compliance monitoring
options.b: Strategic alignment and value delivery through customer-focused innovation
options.c: Resource consolidation and application standardisation across service units
options.d: Infrastructure optimisation and decentralised workforce governance coordination

questions.answer_text: Strategic alignment and value delivery through customer-focused innovation
questions.explanation: The initiative ties technology to a business goal (financial inclusion) and delivers measurable customer value.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: How does IT contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?

options.a: By physically constructing many new roads
options.b: By supporting education, health, and governance
options.c: By significantly reducing all staff salaries
options.d: By completely eliminating all paper use

questions.answer_text: By supporting education, health, and governance
questions.explanation: IT supports SDG 4 (education), health outcomes and SDG 16 (transparent governance) rather than infrastructure construction or cost-cutting.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Within an operational resilience exercise at Zenith Bank Nigeria Plc, cybersecurity analysts identified phishing attacks targeting online banking customers. Which IT management principle is MOST directly involved in mitigating this threat?

options.a: Performance optimisation through centralised monitoring dashboards
options.b: Risk management through proactive identification of cybersecurity threats
options.c: Resource coordination through strategic outsourcing of IT operations
options.d: Value delivery through customer acquisition and product diversification

questions.answer_text: Risk management through proactive identification of cybersecurity threats
questions.explanation: Identifying and controlling threats such as phishing before they cause damage is the risk management principle.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: During a digital transformation review conducted at Access Bank Nigeria Plc, stakeholders observed that newly deployed platforms failed because employees continued using manual processes. Which challenge of IT management BEST explains this outcome?

options.a: Regulatory uncertainty involving overlapping financial compliance directives
options.b: Infrastructure instability caused by insufficient cloud migration strategies
options.c: Cultural resistance resulting from low digital literacy and workflow habits
options.d: Performance measurement failures involving weak service-level agreements

questions.answer_text: Cultural resistance resulting from low digital literacy and workflow habits
questions.explanation: Staff reverting to manual routines signals cultural resistance to change, not an infrastructure or regulatory issue.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Following repeated downtime incidents across enterprise platforms at MTN Nigeria Communications Plc, infrastructure architects proposed migration to Amazon Web Services Incorporated (AWS). Which IT management principle primarily supports this decision?

options.a: Resource management and operational continuity through scalable infrastructure
options.b: Workforce rationalisation through reduction of internal technical personnel
options.c: Organisational restructuring through decentralised departmental reporting lines
options.d: Governance optimisation through stricter software procurement procedures

questions.answer_text: Resource management and operational continuity through scalable infrastructure
questions.explanation: Moving to scalable cloud infrastructure addresses downtime by using IT resources more efficiently and keeping operations continuous.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Following implementation of centralised reporting systems at Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS), administrators emphasised transparent access to operational records and transaction histories. Which benefit of IT management is MOST evident?

options.a: Flexibility through decentralised vendor management and outsourcing models
options.b: Scalability through elastic allocation of distributed computing resources
options.c: Innovation through artificial intelligence experimentation and virtualisation
options.d: Transparency through centralised repositories and track-and-trace systems

questions.answer_text: Transparency through centralised repositories and track-and-trace systems
questions.explanation: Centralised repositories with traceable records provide transparency and accountability.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: What does the evolution of enterprise IT reflect?

options.a: Growth from isolated systems to ecosystem-driven platforms
options.b: A shift from cloud to mainframe computing
options.c: A significant decrease in global digital dependency
options.d: The complete end of digital transformation efforts

questions.answer_text: Growth from isolated systems to ecosystem-driven platforms
questions.explanation: Enterprise IT moved from mainframes and silos through client-server, internet and cloud to integrated digital ecosystems.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Following ransomware preparedness exercises conducted at Rack Centre Data Infrastructure Limited, executives instructed IT teams to create formal disaster recovery documentation and incident response procedures. Which management function is MOST directly demonstrated?

options.a: Planning through development of risk mitigation and recovery strategies
options.b: Staffing through workforce expansion and specialised talent acquisition efforts
options.c: Organising through departmental restructuring and reporting alignment controls
options.d: Directing through continuous employee engagement and communication activities

questions.answer_text: Planning through development of risk mitigation and recovery strategies
questions.explanation: Preparing documented recovery strategies before an incident is the planning function.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Throughout a digital governance assessment at Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), reviewers discovered fragmented technology assets lacking centralised oversight. Which managerial function would BEST address this problem?

options.a: Controlling through operational monitoring and variance correction strategies
options.b: Organising through structured coordination of tasks and decision authority
options.c: Staffing through employee recruitment and performance incentive restructuring
options.d: Directing through motivational leadership and communication enhancement plans

questions.answer_text: Organising through structured coordination of tasks and decision authority
questions.explanation: Organising defines roles, reporting lines and decision authority, which brings fragmented assets under central oversight.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Beyond routine infrastructure upgrades at MainOne Cable Company Nigeria Limited, executives approved enterprise-wide cloud migration because existing systems could no longer support rapid service expansion. Which IT management benefit MOST strongly influenced this decision?

options.a: Resource balancing through departmental budget reduction initiatives
options.b: Governance enforcement through centralised compliance verification procedures
options.c: Scalability through elastic expansion of computing and storage resources
options.d: Transparency through digitised monitoring of customer service operations

questions.answer_text: Scalability through elastic expansion of computing and storage resources
questions.explanation: Cloud elasticity lets capacity grow with demand, which is scalability.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Across multiple branches of First Bank of Nigeria Limited, analysts noticed that inconsistent internet connectivity disrupted access to centralised customer systems. Which IT management challenge BEST explains this situation?

options.a: Strategic misalignment involving poor customer acquisition planning decisions
options.b: Infrastructural instability involving unreliable communication network availability
options.c: Governance complexity involving overlapping software licensing agreements
options.d: Organisational resistance caused by inadequate employee motivation strategies

questions.answer_text: Infrastructural instability involving unreliable communication network availability
questions.explanation: Unreliable connectivity is an infrastructure instability challenge.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a key function of IT management?

options.a: Physical filing of paper documents
options.b: Strategic alignment of technology goals
options.c: Manual data entry and processing
options.d: Marketing campaigns and promotions

questions.answer_text: Strategic alignment of technology goals
questions.explanation: Aligning technology goals with business strategy is a core IT management function.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Following operational reviews at Dell Technologies Infrastructure Solutions, executives approved enterprise-wide virtualisation to improve resource utilisation and infrastructure efficiency. The primary IT management benefit targeted by this investment relates to:

options.a: Flexibility through adaptive infrastructure and optimised resource allocation
options.b: Organisational isolation through segmentation of operational communication flows
options.c: Regulatory simplification through reduction of compliance monitoring activities
options.d: Workforce decentralisation through independent regional support structures

questions.answer_text: Flexibility through adaptive infrastructure and optimised resource allocation
questions.explanation: Virtualisation lets infrastructure adapt and resources be reallocated efficiently, which is flexibility.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A state government installs biometric attendance devices for civil servants but never links them to payroll or employee records, leaving the data unused. Which IT management principle has been MOST clearly violated?

options.a: Strategic alignment, because the technology was not integrated with organisational objectives and produced no strategic use
options.b: Resource management, because the devices were procured without central purchasing by a dedicated IT unit
options.c: Performance measurement, because no uptime or incident-frequency indicators were defined for the devices
options.d: Risk management, because biometric data was not protected through encryption and role-based access

questions.answer_text: Strategic alignment, because the technology was not integrated with organisational objectives and produced no strategic use
questions.explanation: Isolated data with no link to payroll shows technology that does not serve a business objective, which is a strategic alignment failure.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A Nigerian company spends heavily on an HR software suite, yet staff still submit leave forms on paper and no benefit can be traced to the investment. Which principle explains why this outcome is a failure?

options.a: Strategic alignment, because HR software should always be selected by the board of directors
options.b: Resource management, because software licences should be shared across several departments
options.c: Value delivery, because IT investments must yield real, measurable and traceable returns
options.d: Risk management, because unused software exposes the firm to compliance violations and downtime

questions.answer_text: Value delivery, because IT investments must yield real, measurable and traceable returns
questions.explanation: Value delivery requires that benefits (time saved, better decisions, trust) are real and traceable; unused tools waste money.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: After several Nigerian banks suffered fraud caused by weak password practices, the Central Bank of Nigeria issued a directive on multi-factor authentication. Which principle is turned from theory into policy?

options.a: Value delivery, through measurable returns on authentication investments
options.b: Resource management, through centralising authentication hardware procurement
options.c: Risk management, through identifying and controlling threats before they cause damage
options.d: Performance measurement, through tracking resolution times for login incidents

questions.answer_text: Risk management, through identifying and controlling threats before they cause damage
questions.explanation: The directive introduces a control against an identified threat, which is the risk management principle in action.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A secondary school group allows each department to buy its own printers, laptops and internet bundles, creating incompatible devices and duplicated costs. Which remedy BEST reflects the resource management principle?

options.a: A formal risk register recording hardware theft and power surges
options.b: Dashboards that track uptime and user satisfaction for each department
options.c: A roadmap that links every purchase to the school's mission statement
options.d: Central procurement and shared resources maintained by a dedicated IT unit

questions.answer_text: Central procurement and shared resources maintained by a dedicated IT unit
questions.explanation: Resource management aims for efficient, effective use of IT assets; central procurement removes duplication and incompatibility.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: An e-commerce platform notices that a one-second delay in page response costs it millions in lost sales and so monitors cart abandonment and app crashes constantly. Which principle is MOST directly demonstrated?

options.a: Performance measurement, by tracking defined metrics to know whether IT is delivering
options.b: Strategic alignment, by ensuring IT leaders attend board meetings
options.c: Resource management, by outsourcing specialised roles such as database optimisation
options.d: Risk management, by enforcing role-based access to customer records

questions.answer_text: Performance measurement, by tracking defined metrics to know whether IT is delivering
questions.explanation: Tracking uptime, response and abandonment metrics lets the firm judge whether systems are working, which is performance measurement.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A university IT director states that "we need a new payroll system within six months." At which level of planning is this statement MOST accurately classified?

options.a: Operational planning, because it describes daily execution tasks
options.b: Tactical planning, because it sets a mid-term priority
options.c: Contingency planning, because it responds to an unexpected failure
options.d: Strategic planning, because it expresses long-term organisational vision

questions.answer_text: Tactical planning, because it sets a mid-term priority
questions.explanation: Planning occurs at three levels; a six-month priority is tactical, five-year visions are strategic and daily tasks are operational.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: The leadership of a federal agency declares: "We will fully digitise student records in five years." Which statement about this declaration is CORRECT?

options.a: It is a controlling activity because it compares actual performance with targets
options.b: It is an operational plan because it concerns the daily handling of records
options.c: It is a staffing decision because it defines the skills required in the registry
options.d: It is a strategic-level plan that sets long-term vision for later tactical and operational plans

questions.answer_text: It is a strategic-level plan that sets long-term vision for later tactical and operational plans
questions.explanation: A five-year digitisation goal is long-term vision, the strategic level of planning.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: An IT audit team runs checks to confirm that only authorised users access sensitive data and compares actual spend with the procurement plan. Which management function is being performed?

options.a: Controlling, as monitoring performance and correcting deviations from plans
options.b: Directing, as motivating the team and removing blockers to productivity
options.c: Planning, as setting goals and strategies for future change
options.d: Organising, as defining roles, responsibilities and reporting hierarchies

questions.answer_text: Controlling, as monitoring performance and correcting deviations from plans
questions.explanation: Controlling is the feedback mechanism that audits, monitors and corrects performance against plans and policy.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: To reduce loss of skilled engineers to overseas remote jobs, a Lagos firm introduces paid certifications, mentorship programmes and career paths. Which IT management function does this represent?

options.a: Staffing, through training and retention of competent people
options.b: Controlling, through auditing staff access rights to sensitive systems
options.c: Directing, through setting performance targets and holding daily check-ins
options.d: Organising, through creating a helpdesk and network engineering roles

questions.answer_text: Staffing, through training and retention of competent people
questions.explanation: Staffing covers selecting, training and retaining people; certifications and career paths target retention.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: An IT department adopts Scrum, runs sprints, holds team check-ins and removes obstacles that slow developers. Which function of IT management is MOST evident?

options.a: Planning, through five-year strategic roadmapping
options.b: Organising, through formal reporting hierarchies and governance structures
options.c: Directing, through leadership, motivation and daily guidance
options.d: Staffing, through recruitment and talent retention

questions.answer_text: Directing, through leadership, motivation and daily guidance
questions.explanation: Directing is the leadership function: setting targets, check-ins, listening and removing blockers.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: In a growing firm, every employee holds admin access and nobody knows who is responsible for data backups, so backups are skipped. Which function would MOST directly fix this?

options.a: Directing, by publishing motivational communication plans
options.b: Organising, by defining roles, responsibilities and workflows
options.c: Controlling, by comparing system performance with benchmarks
options.d: Staffing, by recruiting more engineers with certifications

questions.answer_text: Organising, by defining roles, responsibilities and workflows
questions.explanation: Unclear ownership and over-broad access are structural problems solved by organising roles and responsibilities.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: The National Identity Management Commission must integrate biometric data, maintain nationwide uptime for registration and comply with privacy laws. Which sector-specific emphasis of IT management does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: NGOs, where systems must work offline and in low-bandwidth rural areas
options.b: SMEs, where informal IT depends on a few tech-savvy individuals without documentation
options.c: Government agencies, where the focus is security, compliance, transparency and reliable public portals
options.d: Startups, where IT managers double as developers and prioritise rapid feature release

questions.answer_text: Government agencies, where the focus is security, compliance, transparency and reliable public portals
questions.explanation: Public-sector IT stresses security, compliance, transparency and uptime for citizen-facing services.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A Lagos health-tech CTO launches apps on cloud services without buying hardware, holds daily scrums and iterates rapidly with a very small team. Which statement BEST characterises this context?

options.a: A startup environment, agile and scalability-focused but limited by staff and release pressure
options.b: An educational institution environment, balancing legacy systems with new student platforms
options.c: An SME environment, run informally with no documentation and no formal IT strategy
options.d: A government agency environment, dominated by procurement bureaucracy and compliance reviews

questions.answer_text: A startup environment, agile and scalability-focused but limited by staff and release pressure
questions.explanation: Startups use agile methods and cloud services to scale quickly while facing limited staff and high pressure.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A small trading company has no dedicated IT manager; a tech-savvy employee "figures things out," and there are no documented procedures or backup policies. What is the MOST significant long-term risk?

options.a: Excessive bureaucracy that slows every software purchase and delays routine upgrades each year
options.b: Over-centralised governance that slows decision-making across several competing departments
options.c: Dependence on single individuals, with no documentation, backups or strategy to fall back on
options.d: Overinvestment in cloud services whose recurring fees quickly exceed the small annual IT budget

questions.answer_text: Dependence on single individuals, with no documentation, backups or strategy to fall back on
questions.explanation: Informal SME IT works short term but creates risk through key-person dependence and absent documentation and backups.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A maternal health NGO deploys mobile apps in remote clinics that sync later with cloud dashboards. Which design requirement is MOST critical for such an organisation?

options.a: Systems that work in low-bandwidth or offline environments
options.b: A formal CAB to approve every software change
options.c: A large internal IT department with specialised roles
options.d: Enterprise-wide ERP integration across all departments

questions.answer_text: Systems that work in low-bandwidth or offline environments
questions.explanation: NGOs operate in rural areas, so offline-capable and low-bandwidth systems are essential.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A national digital strategy aims to use transparent e-governance platforms to reduce corruption and increase citizen engagement. Which Sustainable Development Goal does this MOST directly support?

options.a: SDG 8, Decent work and economic growth
options.b: SDG 9, Industry, innovation and infrastructure
options.c: SDG 4, Quality education
options.d: SDG 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions

questions.answer_text: SDG 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions
questions.explanation: Transparent digital governance that reduces corruption supports SDG 16.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A ministry moves from rigid departmental silos with command-and-control leadership and paper workflows to cross-departmental teams on shared digital platforms with real-time communication. Which description is MOST accurate?

options.a: A shift from a traditional hierarchical structure to a flat, networked and IT-enabled structure
options.b: A shift from a decentralised structure to a centralised mainframe-based command structure
options.c: An unchanged structure, since technology does not alter supervision, roles or workflows
options.d: A move from agile team working to sequential waterfall operating models across departments

questions.answer_text: A shift from a traditional hierarchical structure to a flat, networked and IT-enabled structure
questions.explanation: IT-enabled structures are flat, networked and cross-functional, contrasting with top-down paper-based hierarchies.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: LifeBank connects blood banks, hospitals and transport systems into one view of supply, delivery and emergencies. Which role of IT in organisational structures does this MOST clearly show?

options.a: Breaking silos through system integration
options.b: Enabling decentralised teams through cloud collaboration
options.c: Creating new organisational roles such as CISO
options.d: Redefining supervision through performance dashboards

questions.answer_text: Breaking silos through system integration
questions.explanation: Linking separate organisations' systems into a single view is integration that breaks down silos.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Departments in a university gain computer labs, email servers and customised HR and finance applications, but the systems cannot exchange data with one another. Which phase of enterprise IT evolution does this describe?

options.a: The client-server era, which gave department-level autonomy but created siloed systems
options.b: The cloud and mobile era, which introduced pay-as-you-go resources
options.c: The mainframe era, which centralised computing for trained technical staff
options.d: The digital ecosystem era, which relies on open APIs and shared data governance

questions.answer_text: The client-server era, which gave department-level autonomy but created siloed systems
questions.explanation: The client-server era boosted departmental collaboration yet produced siloed systems without system-wide integration.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A bank launches full-scale online banking, universities build e-portals and government offers online result checking. Which phase does this represent and what was its main shift?

options.a: Mainframe era, when batch processing served only back-office functions for trained staff
options.b: Client-server era, when LANs gave staff shared access to files, printers and applications
options.c: Internet and web-based era, when IT became an external gateway to customers and the public
options.d: Cloud and mobile era, when BYOD, DevOps and pay-as-you-go computing resources emerged

questions.answer_text: Internet and web-based era, when IT became an external gateway to customers and the public
questions.explanation: Web-based services opened IT to customers and the public, changing it from internal tool to external gateway.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: A Lagos fintech CTO must make internal banking systems communicate flawlessly with Paystack, Remita, regulators and tax APIs, while also moving beyond perimeter defence. Which statement BEST describes this expanded role?

options.a: The IT manager limits responsibility to internal systems because partner platforms secure their own APIs
options.b: The IT manager evaluates hardware procurement for central data centres and leaves integration to partners
options.c: The IT manager concentrates on keeping on-premise servers running and fixing individual user issues
options.d: The IT manager acts as an ecosystem integrator using API management, zero-trust security and stakeholder collaboration

questions.answer_text: The IT manager acts as an ecosystem integrator using API management, zero-trust security and stakeholder collaboration
questions.explanation: In digital ecosystems each integration is a potential vulnerability, so managers integrate systems, adopt zero-trust and API security and collaborate across stakeholders.

questions.module_title: Introduction to Information Technology Management
questions.question: Which combination of obligations MOST accurately defines the IT manager's responsibility as data custodian in a digital ecosystem governed by NDPR and GDPR?

options.a: Data minimisation, secure storage with controlled access, and consent-based sharing across the data lifecycle
options.b: Perimeter-only protection, annual audits and informal consent collected after processing has begun
options.c: Outsourcing all accountability to cloud providers and removing internal custodianship of data
options.d: Maximum data collection for analytics, open sharing with partners and indefinite retention of records

questions.answer_text: Data minimisation, secure storage with controlled access, and consent-based sharing across the data lifecycle
questions.explanation: Modern privacy laws expect collecting only what is needed, securing it, and sharing on consent while managing the data lifecycle.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: What is the main goal of aligning IT strategy with business objectives?

options.a: To ensure investments support strategic goals
options.b: To reduce the annual IT budget
options.c: To create many new employee jobs
options.d: To enable various corporate marketing efforts

questions.answer_text: To ensure investments support strategic goals
questions.explanation: Alignment ensures every IT investment contributes to measurable business goals rather than existing for its own sake.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Amid increasing digital competition across Nigerian banking platforms, executives at Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO) proposed integrating predictive analytics into customer service channels. Which IT management principle is MOST directly demonstrated by this initiative?

options.a: Performance measurement through operational dashboards and reporting controls
options.b: Strategic alignment through technology-enabled customer experience innovation
options.c: Resource allocation through workforce restructuring and procurement controls
options.d: Risk mitigation through compliance enforcement and infrastructure monitoring

questions.answer_text: Strategic alignment through technology-enabled customer experience innovation
questions.explanation: Using analytics to improve customer experience ties IT directly to competitive business strategy.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A Lagos-based FMCG distributor automates inventory management and route optimisation, cutting fuel costs and eliminating stockouts after an IT strategy review. Which reason for having an IT strategy does this MOST directly support?

options.a: Driving strategic innovation through rapid feature rollout and microservices-based product launches
options.b: Improving customer satisfaction through seamless digital experiences and faster issue resolution
options.c: Reducing operational costs and inefficiency through process automation and system integration
options.d: Managing regulatory compliance through integrated security and data protection measures

questions.answer_text: Reducing operational costs and inefficiency through process automation and system integration
questions.explanation: Automation and integration that cut fuel cost and stockouts illustrate IT reducing operational costs and inefficiency.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Edo State's e-governance strategy made its civil service paperless, so staff continued working from home when COVID-19 struck. Which strategic benefit of IT does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: Cost leadership through lower salary bills
options.b: Customer stickiness through personalised loyalty features
options.c: Agility and future-readiness through modular, adaptable systems
options.d: Reduced vendor dependence through open-source software

questions.answer_text: Agility and future-readiness through modular, adaptable systems
questions.explanation: Being able to continue operations during sudden disruption shows agility and readiness for change.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A Lagos hospital runs four unintegrated packages for patient management, billing, diagnostics and reporting, and then adopts a modular HMIS under one umbrella. Which component of IT strategy is MOST directly applied?

options.a: Application portfolio management, by rationalising redundant and unintegrated applications
options.b: Human capital planning, by auditing staff IT skills and building competency frameworks
options.c: Enterprise architecture, by defining network, database and cloud infrastructure standards
options.d: Governance and decision-making, by setting up an IT steering committee for approvals

questions.answer_text: Application portfolio management, by rationalising redundant and unintegrated applications
questions.explanation: Application portfolio management decides which apps are essential, redundant, integrated or retired, avoiding application bloat.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: The Corporate Affairs Commission re-architected its registration platform to integrate with NIN, BVN and CAC registration APIs, enabling business registration within 24 to 48 hours. Which strategic attribute of enterprise architecture is MOST evident?

options.a: Resilience, because systems recover automatically from failure
options.b: Interoperability, because systems can talk to one another
options.c: Cost leadership, because licences are cheaper
options.d: Scalability, because users can grow into the millions

questions.answer_text: Interoperability, because systems can talk to one another
questions.explanation: Integrating with NIN, BVN and other registries demonstrates interoperability between systems.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Sterling Bank's digital-first model was approved with buy-in from every department so that transformation aligned with customer journey mapping, service innovation and staff upskilling. Which element of IT strategy is MOST directly demonstrated?

options.a: Business alignment, through early stakeholder engagement across business units
options.b: Budgeting and investment planning, through capital and operating expenditure models
options.c: Data strategy, through data quality, integration and analytics maturity
options.d: Cybersecurity and risk management, through penetration testing and access controls

questions.answer_text: Business alignment, through early stakeholder engagement across business units
questions.explanation: Consulting business unit heads and frontline staff when forming the strategy is the stakeholder engagement part of business alignment.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Under Central Bank of Nigeria mandates, banks maintain IT Steering Committees that report on cybersecurity, data protection and business continuity. Which strategy component do these committees primarily represent?

options.a: Application portfolio management that retires redundant software and integrates overlapping tools
options.b: Data analytics maturity through descriptive, predictive and prescriptive modelling of customer data
options.c: Human capital building through certification programmes and continuous learning paths for staff
options.d: Governance and decision-making structures that ensure alignment and executive accountability

questions.answer_text: Governance and decision-making structures that ensure alignment and executive accountability
questions.explanation: IT governance defines who decides, how priorities are set and how risks are managed; steering committees embody this.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A data strategy review asks: "Can our systems exchange and combine data across the organisation without manual re-entry?" Which pillar of a sound data strategy is being assessed?

options.a: Data integration
options.b: Data governance
options.c: Data quality
options.d: Regulatory compliance

questions.answer_text: Data integration
questions.explanation: The question concerns whether systems share and combine data, which is the data integration pillar.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: After a ransomware attack locked customers out of mobile banking for 48 hours, a microfinance bank adopted cloud-based backups, endpoint detection and monthly penetration testing. Which strategy component does this MOST directly exemplify?

options.a: Cybersecurity and risk management as a core, built-in element of the IT strategy
options.b: Business alignment through early stakeholder consultation across every business unit
options.c: Application portfolio management through sunsetting of redundant legacy applications
options.d: Human capital planning through IT skills audits and competency frameworks for staff

questions.answer_text: Cybersecurity and risk management as a core, built-in element of the IT strategy
questions.explanation: Backups, endpoint detection and penetration testing are security controls included in the cybersecurity and risk component.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Dangote Group uses SAP Ariba for real-time bidding, supplier performance tracking and contract lifecycle management, making it hard for any single supplier to dictate terms. In Porter's Five Forces terms, IT is:

options.a: Reducing the bargaining power of customers through loyalty systems and personalisation
options.b: Defending against substitutes through digital enhancements to existing physical services
options.c: Weakening the bargaining power of suppliers through transparency and access to alternatives
options.d: Raising entry barriers for new competitors through proprietary platforms and brand equity

questions.answer_text: Weakening the bargaining power of suppliers through transparency and access to alternatives
questions.explanation: E-procurement and performance visibility give buyers more options and information, which reduces supplier power.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Paystack's seamless merchant onboarding, compliance automation and developer-friendly API libraries make it hard for newcomers to match. Which Porter force is IT MOST directly addressing?

options.a: Threat of substitutes, by adding smart dashboards and mobile control to physical services
options.b: Bargaining power of suppliers, by increasing procurement transparency and supplier comparison
options.c: Threat of new entrants, by raising barriers through proprietary platforms and brand equity
options.d: Industry rivalry, by lowering prices through cost leadership and automated back-office operations

questions.answer_text: Threat of new entrants, by raising barriers through proprietary platforms and brand equity
questions.explanation: Proprietary platforms and first-mover credibility create high entry thresholds for new competitors.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A ride-hailing firm uses gamified loyalty rewards, personalisation engines and AI-powered support so that riders rarely switch purely on price. Which force is MOST directly weakened?

options.a: Threat of new entrants
options.b: Industry rivalry among existing firms
options.c: Bargaining power of customers
options.d: Bargaining power of suppliers

questions.answer_text: Bargaining power of customers
questions.explanation: Personalisation and loyalty engagement reduce customers' ability to switch and bargain on price.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Under the Resource-Based View, which IT asset is MOST likely to deliver a sustainable competitive advantage?

options.a: A proprietary AI model trained on years of unique longitudinal customer behaviour data
options.b: A widely available off-the-shelf CRM subscription configured with its default settings
options.c: A mobile app whose interface closely mimics the design of the current market leader
options.d: A corporate website hosted on a popular public cloud platform with standard templates

questions.answer_text: A proprietary AI model trained on years of unique longitudinal customer behaviour data
questions.explanation: RBV values resources that are valuable, rare, inimitable and non-substitutable; unique data-trained models are hard to copy, unlike commodity tools.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A tax agency embeds digital in its culture, uses continuous innovation through agile teams, DevOps and design thinking, and uses data to predict outcomes and adapt strategy. Which stage of the Digital Maturity Model is this?

options.a: Initiate
options.b: Integrated
options.c: Optimised
options.d: Develop

questions.answer_text: Optimised
questions.explanation: Continuous innovation with data used predictively and digital embedded organisationally describes the Optimised stage.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Paga has built over a decade of transactional intelligence from timestamps, geolocation, fraud patterns and spending habits that newer fintechs cannot buy or fast-track. Which type of digital moat is this?

options.a: Platform ecosystem and APIs
options.b: Embedded digital culture
options.c: Proprietary data ecosystem
options.d: Intelligent automation pipeline

questions.answer_text: Proprietary data ecosystem
questions.explanation: Unique, high-volume data accumulated over time that improves predictions and fraud detection is a proprietary data moat.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Hundreds of thousands of merchants depend on Flutterwave's API network linking them to Visa, PayPal and Alipay; a competitor would need dozens of partnerships, uptime guarantees and trust. Which concept BEST explains the moat?

options.a: Differentiation achieved through a superior and more attractive interface design
options.b: Network effects within a platform ecosystem, where value grows as more players integrate
options.c: Technical debt accumulated from rapid feature releases and poorly documented integrations
options.d: Cost leadership achieved through lower manual labour costs and process automation

questions.answer_text: Network effects within a platform ecosystem, where value grows as more players integrate
questions.explanation: The more players use the platform, the more valuable and harder to replace it becomes, which is a network effect moat.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: uLesson uses data on student engagement, dropout points and quiz performance to refine lesson design and pacing, so new entrants can copy its app but not its insights. Which moat capability is MOST evident?

options.a: Intelligent automation pipelines that remove manual work from back-office processes
options.b: Platform APIs and third-party integrations that make switching costly for partners
options.c: Continuous learning and adaptation through feedback loops and data-driven iteration
options.d: Proprietary payment infrastructure that processes transactions faster than competitors

questions.answer_text: Continuous learning and adaptation through feedback loops and data-driven iteration
questions.explanation: Test-measure-improve cycles create a feedback moat of learning that competitors cannot copy by mimicking the interface.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A major Nigerian telecom invests millions in a proprietary CRM, but staff are untrained, managers do not enforce use and records stay in Excel and WhatsApp until the project is abandoned. Which lesson does this case MOST directly teach?

options.a: Migration to the cloud is the standard remedy for low adoption and unenforced system use
options.b: Open-source CRM tools are always superior to proprietary ones and avoid adoption problems
options.c: CRM systems cannot create value in telecommunications because customer data is too fragmented
options.d: Advantage comes from execution quality, user adoption and strategic fit, not from owning technology

questions.answer_text: Advantage comes from execution quality, user adoption and strategic fit, not from owning technology
questions.explanation: The technology was sound; failure came from training, enforcement and adoption, showing that tools alone give no advantage.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Which scenario BEST illustrates competitive advantage rather than competitive parity?

options.a: Using WhatsApp for customer support simply because rival firms have adopted it already
options.b: Launching a mobile app with offline capability and voice support tailored to rural users
options.c: Launching a mobile app because all of the competitors in the market already have one
options.d: Copying the user interface features of the current market leader across all channels

questions.answer_text: Launching a mobile app with offline capability and voice support tailored to rural users
questions.explanation: Parity means matching competitors; advantage means leapfrogging them with differentiated, context-fit capabilities.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Paystack introduced instant merchant verification; within weeks local rivals launched similar flows and the novelty faded. What does this case BEST demonstrate?

options.a: Imitation can be prevented permanently by keeping the user interface strictly confidential
options.b: Isolated features are quickly imitated, so advantage must be layered across data, trust and execution
options.c: Instant verification harms customer trust and should be avoided by all fintech providers
options.d: Regulation prevents fintech firms from differentiating their onboarding and compliance flows

questions.answer_text: Isolated features are quickly imitated, so advantage must be layered across data, trust and execution
questions.explanation: Technical features can be cloned in days, so durable advantage needs deeper layers than a single feature.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Some Nigerian lending platforms use telco usage patterns, app installs and contact lists to estimate creditworthiness, which may penalise low-income or digitally cautious users. Which risk and imperative does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: Imitation risk, requiring faster feature rollout and stronger brand and ecosystem partnerships
options.b: Technical debt, requiring comprehensive documentation, refactoring and integration clean-up work
options.c: Algorithmic bias and financial exclusion, requiring auditable and explainable AI aligned with NDPR
options.d: Vendor lock-in, requiring modular architecture, fallback plans and internal ownership of systems

questions.answer_text: Algorithmic bias and financial exclusion, requiring auditable and explainable AI aligned with NDPR
questions.explanation: Proxy data can reproduce inequality; ethical practice demands transparency, explainable models and NDPR alignment.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A Lagos start-up builds its backend on a third-party automation tool that later shuts down; with no plan B, users experience repeated failures and rebuilding causes churn. Which risk and mitigating lesson fit BEST?

options.a: Cultural resistance, mitigated by internal marketing, incentives and staff training sessions
options.b: Vendor lock-in, mitigated by modularity, fallback plans and internal ownership of key systems
options.c: Algorithmic bias, mitigated by publishing data usage policies and auditing model outputs
options.d: Workforce displacement, mitigated by reskilling programmes and transparent communication

questions.answer_text: Vendor lock-in, mitigated by modularity, fallback plans and internal ownership of key systems
questions.explanation: Dependence on a single third-party stack is lock-in; building modular systems with alternatives reduces the risk.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A fintech lays off 60% of its support team after launching an AI chatbot, and former staff publicly post unpaid severance. Which ethical response would the course MOST support?

options.a: Restrict staff from discussing the layoffs publicly in order to protect the brand image online
options.b: Offer reskilling and transition programmes, communicate transparently and balance efficiency with inclusion
options.c: Replace the chatbot with a vendor product so that blame shifts to the new technology supplier
options.d: Accelerate automation in other departments quickly to recover the lost cost savings and reputation

questions.answer_text: Offer reskilling and transition programmes, communicate transparently and balance efficiency with inclusion
questions.explanation: Ethical firms manage displacement through reskilling, transparency and balancing efficiency with inclusion.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A system quickly processes thousands of customer refunds on a product that should never have been sold. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.a: Neither efficient nor effective, because automation is involved in the process
options.b: Efficient but not effective, because it does not serve the right strategic objective
options.c: Both efficient and effective, because it processes a high volume of refunds quickly
options.d: Effective but not efficient, because the refunds are processed too slowly to matter

questions.answer_text: Efficient but not effective, because it does not serve the right strategic objective
questions.explanation: Efficiency is doing things right with least waste; effectiveness is doing the right things for strategic goals.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: Zenith Bank cut account opening from three to five business days to under ten minutes using automated ID checks, BVN validation and digital signatures. Which dimension of digital operational efficiency is this?

options.a: Resource optimisation
options.b: Process automation
options.c: Self-service platforms
options.d: Real-time visibility

questions.answer_text: Process automation
questions.explanation: Replacing manual KYC verification with automated workflows is process automation.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: MAX.ng tracks vehicle telemetry such as idle time, hard braking and speed variance to cut fuel costs and improve safety. Which efficiency dimension is MOST evident?

options.a: Self-service platforms that reduce dependence on front-line staff and shorten queues
options.b: Resource optimisation, using data to avoid waste of physical and financial resources
options.c: System integration that connects CRM, HR and finance data into one operational fabric
options.d: Process automation that replaces repetitive manual tasks with software workflows

questions.answer_text: Resource optimisation, using data to avoid waste of physical and financial resources
questions.explanation: Telemetry-driven fuel and asset management is resource optimisation.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A Nigerian bank maps its loan process end to end, finds redundant approvals and repeated document checks, automates KYC and sets thresholds to avoid unnecessary escalation, cutting processing from five days to 24 hours. Which methodology is applied?

options.a: Total Quality Management, by embedding quality in every role
options.b: Business Process Reengineering, by radically redesigning the entire business model
options.c: Six Sigma, by using DMAIC to reduce statistical defects
options.d: Lean IT, by identifying value and removing waste through value stream mapping

questions.answer_text: Lean IT, by identifying value and removing waste through value stream mapping
questions.explanation: Mapping the process, removing non-value activities and improving flow are Lean IT practices.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: An FMCG distributor in Ibadan reduces stock mismatch errors from 14% to below 2% by defining the problem, measuring errors, finding root causes, automating error-prone checks and monitoring the fix. Which methodology and sequence apply?

options.a: Six Sigma using DMAIC: Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve and Control
options.b: Kaizen using small daily improvement suggestions from frontline staff in a no-blame culture
options.c: BPR using radical end-to-end redesign instead of incremental process upgrades
options.d: Lean IT using value identification, value stream mapping, flow and a pull system

questions.answer_text: Six Sigma using DMAIC: Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve and Control
questions.explanation: The described steps map to the Six Sigma DMAIC cycle aimed at reducing process variation and defects.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A university IT helpdesk holds a weekly "what didn't go well" roundtable, adds FAQs, prioritises common issues and adjusts peak-hour shifts, cutting ticket resolution time by 35%. Which methodology is this?

options.a: Lean IT, through pull-based control of work and removal of non-value steps
options.b: Six Sigma, through statistical analysis of process variation using DMAIC
options.c: Kaizen, through small, continuous, frontline-led improvements in a non-blame culture
options.d: Business Process Reengineering, through radical end-to-end redesign of workflows

questions.answer_text: Kaizen, through small, continuous, frontline-led improvements in a non-blame culture
questions.explanation: Weekly reflection and small tweaks led by frontline staff reflect Kaizen.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: The Nigeria Customs Service replaced manual clearance with a Single Window platform consolidating declarations, payments, inspections and port clearance across agencies. Which approach does this MOST closely represent?

options.a: Kaizen, by making small incremental improvements suggested daily by frontline staff
options.b: Total Quality Management, by monitoring quality KPIs with closed-loop alerts and dashboards
options.c: Business Process Reengineering, by redesigning processes radically instead of automating inefficiency
options.d: Six Sigma, by controlling defect variation using statistical tools and the DMAIC cycle

questions.answer_text: Business Process Reengineering, by redesigning processes radically instead of automating inefficiency
questions.explanation: BPR rethinks end-to-end processes instead of improving broken ones incrementally.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A Nigerian university assumes students want faster campus internet, but interviews show the real pain is a three-week wait for transcripts and certificates. Which roadmap step does this MOST directly illustrate?

options.a: Set metrics and KPIs by building dashboards in tools such as Power BI or Tableau
options.b: Select appropriate technologies by comparing open-source and commercial options on fit
options.c: Map existing processes by drawing current workflows with Visio, Lucidchart or sticky notes
options.d: Define operational goals by engaging those who live with the problem and solving real pain points

questions.answer_text: Define operational goals by engaging those who live with the problem and solving real pain points
questions.explanation: Starting with clarity about the real problem before choosing tools is step one of the roadmap.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: A government office digitises leave requests and expense reimbursements within two weeks using Google Forms and Sheets before tackling its pension records overhaul. Which principle of the roadmap does this follow?

options.a: Define operational goals by asking staff and customers what slows decisions and causes errors
options.b: Identify quick wins versus long-term projects, so the team can win small and scale smart
options.c: Iterate and scale by running post-implementation reviews and replicating proven workflows
options.d: Plan change management by identifying internal champions and offering structured staff training

questions.answer_text: Identify quick wins versus long-term projects, so the team can win small and scale smart
questions.explanation: Quick wins build confidence and momentum before complex strategic projects.

questions.module_title: IT Strategy and Business Alignment
questions.question: An NGO digitising field reporting in northern Nigeria creates a "Tech Hero of the Month" award and offers mobile data stipends, and adoption triples in three weeks. Which roadmap element is this?

options.a: Set KPIs such as processing-time reduction, error rates and customer satisfaction scores
options.b: Map existing processes by identifying handovers, bottlenecks and repeated data entry
options.c: Select appropriate technologies by weighing licence cost, customisation and vendor support
options.d: Plan the change management through recognition systems, incentives and internal champions

questions.answer_text: Plan the change management through recognition systems, incentives and internal champions
questions.explanation: Recognition and incentives are elements of a change management plan that supports adoption.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: While preparing for a Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) compliance audit, Access Bank Nigeria Plc discovered that customer consent records for data processing were incomplete. Which remediation action best addresses this governance gap?

options.a: Implement a consent management system with audit trails and re-obtain consent
options.b: Continue operations while drafting a retrospective consent letter
options.c: Transfer all customer data to a cloud region outside Nigeria
options.d: Delete all customer data immediately without notification

questions.answer_text: Implement a consent management system with audit trails and re-obtain consent
questions.explanation: Compliance requires documented, auditable, consent-based processing; retrospective letters, offshoring or silent deletion do not fix the gap.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: During organisational continuity reviews at Cisco Systems Incorporated, cybersecurity teams highlighted the growing risk of phishing attacks targeting enterprise communication systems. The most appropriate IT management response would prioritise:

options.a: Decentralised infrastructure governance through independent regional oversight
options.b: Reduced compliance monitoring through simplified operational reporting models
options.c: Workforce restructuring through elimination of internal security personnel
options.d: Proactive risk mitigation through cybersecurity awareness and protection controls

questions.answer_text: Proactive risk mitigation through cybersecurity awareness and protection controls
questions.explanation: Phishing is best countered by proactive controls and user awareness; weakening oversight or removing security staff increases risk.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: What framework is best suited for information security management and is certifiable?

options.a: ISO/IEC 38500 standard
options.b: ISO/IEC 27001 standard
options.c: The ITIL framework
options.d: COBIT control standards

questions.answer_text: ISO/IEC 27001 standard
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 specifies a certifiable information security management system.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which principle is part of both GDPR and Nigeria's NDPR regulations?

options.a: Free sharing with any third parties
options.b: Mandatory use of open source software
options.c: Encryption is never required for privacy
options.d: Rights to access and delete data

questions.answer_text: Rights to access and delete data
questions.explanation: Both regimes give data subjects rights over their data, including access and erasure.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: In the context of IT Service Management (ITSM), what is the primary function of a service desk?

options.a: Logging and resolving technical incidents
options.b: Overseeing company payroll management systems
options.c: Designing new corporate marketing strategies
options.d: Reviewing annual budgets for projects

questions.answer_text: Logging and resolving technical incidents
questions.explanation: The service desk is the single point of contact that logs, categorises, escalates and resolves incidents and requests.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which IT governance framework is primarily strategic and focuses on enabling executive decision-making?

options.a: ISO/IEC 38500 standard
options.b: The ITIL framework
options.c: The COBIT framework
options.d: The PCI-DSS standard

questions.answer_text: ISO/IEC 38500 standard
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 38500 provides principle-based, board-level guidance for governing IT; ITIL is operational and PCI-DSS is a payment security standard.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes IT governance from IT service management (ITSM)?

options.a: Governance manages daily incident tickets and queues, while ITSM sets the board's technology priorities
options.b: Governance and ITSM are identical terms describing the same set of ITIL operational processes
options.c: Governance concerns only information security, while ITSM concerns only hardware procurement and leasing
options.d: Governance sets direction, priorities and accountability, while ITSM delivers consistent daily services within it

questions.answer_text: Governance sets direction, priorities and accountability, while ITSM delivers consistent daily services within it
questions.explanation: Governance defines who decides and what the targets are; ITSM drives the operations that reach those targets.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A bank's IT office states that its framework distinguishes governance (evaluate, direct and monitor) from management (plan, build, run and monitor) and covers the enterprise end to end. Which framework is being described?

options.a: ITIL v4, centred on the Service Value System
options.b: ISO/IEC 27001, for information security management systems
options.c: PCI-DSS, for payment card data protection
options.d: COBIT, developed by ISACA

questions.answer_text: COBIT, developed by ISACA
questions.explanation: COBIT separates governance from management and applies a single integrated end-to-end framework.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: What BEST distinguishes ITIL 4 from earlier ITIL versions?

options.a: It removes continual improvement in favour of fixed annual audits of every service process
options.b: It replaces service management with a pure information security certification standard
options.c: It mandates rigid adoption of every process by all organisations regardless of size or context
options.d: It introduces the Service Value System, integrating Lean, Agile and DevOps with an end-to-end value focus

questions.answer_text: It introduces the Service Value System, integrating Lean, Agile and DevOps with an end-to-end value focus
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 shifts from a process-only view to the Service Value System and value co-creation.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A university IT team wants to rebuild every service process from scratch, ignoring existing processes that work. Which ITIL guiding principle would MOST directly challenge this approach?

options.a: Optimise and automate
options.b: Start where you are
options.c: Focus on value
options.d: Collaborate and promote visibility

questions.answer_text: Start where you are
questions.explanation: "Start where you are" advises assessing and reusing existing services and processes instead of starting over.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A customer-service-oriented fintech start-up struggles with slow and inconsistent customer support. Which framework would the course suggest as the MOST relevant starting point?

options.a: PCI-DSS, to protect cardholder data through access restriction and network monitoring
options.b: ISO/IEC 27001, to obtain independent certification of its information security management system
options.c: ITIL, to improve service delivery processes such as incident management and the service desk
options.d: COBIT, to satisfy regulators' requirements for enterprise-wide governance and board reporting

questions.answer_text: ITIL, to improve service delivery processes such as incident management and the service desk
questions.explanation: ITIL focuses on service lifecycle and operational practices, suiting service-quality pain points.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A hospital group wants a formal, independently certifiable information security management system. Which choice is MOST appropriate?

options.a: ISO/IEC 27001
options.b: ISO/IEC 38500
options.c: COBIT process capability levels
options.d: ITIL 4 Foundation

questions.answer_text: ISO/IEC 27001
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 is certifiable for information security; ISO/IEC 38500 is principle-based governance guidance.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Why might an organisation adopt more than one IT governance framework?

options.a: Regulators forbid the use of a single framework in any bank, telecom or public agency
options.b: Frameworks address different needs, for example COBIT for governance, ITIL for services and ISO 27001 for security
options.c: Frameworks are mutually exclusive and are replaced by newer ones every single year
options.d: Multiple frameworks remove the need to define roles, responsibilities and approval levels

questions.answer_text: Frameworks address different needs, for example COBIT for governance, ITIL for services and ISO 27001 for security
questions.explanation: Frameworks are complementary, so combining them gives a tailored approach.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A Nigerian business process outsourcing firm serves customers resident in the European Union. Which statement about GDPR is CORRECT?

options.a: It applies because the firm serves or targets EU residents, even though it is based outside the EU
options.b: It applies only to companies headquartered inside the European Union and to their subsidiaries
options.c: It does not apply to outsourcing firms because they only process data on behalf of clients
options.d: It applies only when the personal data is physically stored in a data centre in the EU

questions.answer_text: It applies because the firm serves or targets EU residents, even though it is based outside the EU
questions.explanation: GDPR has extraterritorial scope when organisations serve or target EU residents.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Under the GDPR, an organisation discovers a personal data breach. Which obligation applies?

options.a: Wait until the annual audit and then inform the regulator in the next compliance report
options.b: Notify only the shareholders and leave regulators to discover the incident independently
options.c: Notify the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware, where required
options.d: Delete all of the affected records before any report is made to avoid further exposure

questions.answer_text: Notify the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware, where required
questions.explanation: The GDPR requires breach notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A Nigerian health-tech firm processes electronic patient records for a United States hospital client. Which regulation's safeguards for electronic protected health information (ePHI) are MOST relevant?

options.a: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
options.b: NDPR
options.c: PCI-DSS
options.d: HIPAA

questions.answer_text: HIPAA
questions.explanation: HIPAA governs confidentiality, integrity and availability of ePHI in US health data.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which statement about the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) is CORRECT?

options.a: It was introduced by the European Commission in 2018 as binding law for all member states
options.b: It was introduced in January 2019 by NITDA to promote data privacy and protect individuals' rights
options.c: It was enacted by the US Department of Health and Human Services to govern patient records
options.d: It applies only to financial institutions regulated by the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.answer_text: It was introduced in January 2019 by NITDA to promote data privacy and protect individuals' rights
questions.explanation: The NDPR was issued by NITDA in January 2019 as a national data privacy framework.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A Nigerian payment processor stores, processes and transmits cardholder data. Which standard primarily governs its security controls such as restricted access, network monitoring and vulnerability testing?

options.a: HIPAA
options.b: ISO/IEC 38500
options.c: PCI-DSS
options.d: GDPR Article 17

questions.answer_text: PCI-DSS
questions.explanation: PCI-DSS is the industry data security standard for organisations handling payment card data.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: After a data breach, investigators need to determine who accessed particular customer records, when, and what they did. Which control provides this?

options.a: Audit trails with detailed system logs
options.b: Mandatory annual compliance training
options.c: A published acceptable use policy
options.d: A business impact analysis

questions.answer_text: Audit trails with detailed system logs
questions.explanation: An audit trail is a chronological record that supports accountability and traceability.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: In one environment, access permissions are centrally set according to classification labels and individual users cannot change them. Which access control model is this?

options.a: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
options.b: Peer-to-peer sharing
options.c: Discretionary Access Control (DAC)
options.d: Open access with after-the-fact logging

questions.answer_text: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
questions.explanation: Under MAC, access is governed by centrally enforced rules and classifications rather than user discretion.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A mid-sized Nigerian company begins a compliance programme but does not know what personal data it holds. Which first step is MOST appropriate?

options.a: Appoint external auditors only after a regulator has opened a complaint about the firm
options.b: Delete older records quickly so that the compliance burden and risk exposure are reduced
options.c: Conduct a comprehensive audit of what personal data is collected, where it is stored and who can access it
options.d: Purchase a compliance software suite first and assess the data practices at a later date

questions.answer_text: Conduct a comprehensive audit of what personal data is collected, where it is stored and who can access it
questions.explanation: A baseline audit and risk assessment identify gaps and prioritise remediation.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A Nigerian lender shares customer data with a cloud vendor. Which measure BEST extends its compliance obligations to the vendor?

options.a: Rely on the vendor's marketing statements about the strength of its security controls
options.b: Assume that the vendor carries all legal liability once the data has been transferred
options.c: Share only the customer names and keep other fields to avoid any legal obligations
options.d: Contractually require the same standards through data processing agreements, due diligence and audits

questions.answer_text: Contractually require the same standards through data processing agreements, due diligence and audits
questions.explanation: Third-party providers must be bound by contract, due diligence and regular audits to the same compliance standards.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST example of operational IT risk?

options.a: A competitor launching a better mobile app and attracting the firm's existing customers
options.b: A prolonged power failure and untrained staff causing a system to stop during peak transaction hours
options.c: A misjudged technology investment that does not support the organisation's strategy
options.d: A hacker deploying ransomware that encrypts the files of a hospital information system

questions.answer_text: A prolonged power failure and untrained staff causing a system to stop during peak transaction hours
questions.explanation: Operational risks arise from day-to-day functioning, such as power, backups, maintenance and staff training.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A company's IT investment in a new platform fails to match its business objectives and erodes long-term competitiveness because of poor planning and resistance to change. Which type of IT risk is this?

options.a: Compliance risk
options.b: Operational risk
options.c: Cybersecurity risk
options.d: Strategic risk

questions.answer_text: Strategic risk
questions.explanation: Strategic risk emerges when technology initiatives fail to align with business objectives.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders the Risk Management Lifecycle described in the course?

options.a: Risk mitigation, risk identification, risk transfer, then risk acceptance and closure
options.b: Risk monitoring, risk avoidance, risk identification, then risk assessment and closure
options.c: Risk assessment, risk insurance, risk reporting, then risk identification and mitigation
options.d: Risk identification, risk assessment and analysis, risk mitigation, then monitoring and reporting

questions.answer_text: Risk identification, risk assessment and analysis, risk mitigation, then monitoring and reporting
questions.explanation: The lifecycle begins with identifying risks, then assessing, mitigating and monitoring them continuously.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: On a risk heat map, a ransomware threat with high likelihood and high impact falls in the red zone. What does this require?

options.a: Acceptance with minimal oversight
options.b: Immediate attention and mitigation
options.c: Regular monitoring only
options.d: Removal from the risk register

questions.answer_text: Immediate attention and mitigation
questions.explanation: Red-zone risks demand immediate attention; amber needs regular monitoring and green is acceptable with monitoring.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A bank decides not to host highly sensitive customer data with a third-party cloud provider because the risk is considered unacceptable. Which risk response is this?

options.a: Risk avoidance
options.b: Risk transfer
options.c: Risk acceptance
options.d: Risk reduction

questions.answer_text: Risk avoidance
questions.explanation: Changing plans to eliminate the risk entirely is risk avoidance.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: After a ransomware incident, EagleTrust Bank concluded that weak employee behaviour and weaknesses at a vendor contributed to the breach. Which lessons does this support?

options.a: Technology controls alone are sufficient to prevent ransomware incidents in banks
options.b: Cyber risk should be managed separately from enterprise-wide risk by the security team
options.c: Human-centred risk management and third-party oversight must be part of enterprise risk management
options.d: Vendors are always fully responsible for the bank's risk exposure and its consequences

questions.answer_text: Human-centred risk management and third-party oversight must be part of enterprise risk management
questions.explanation: The case shows that employee behaviour and third-party weaknesses must be part of risk management.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A service desk's first-line agent cannot resolve a database corruption and passes it to the database administration team. Later, because an SLA breach is imminent, the matter is passed to the IT manager. Which escalation types are these, in order?
