options.a: Functional escalation, then hierarchical escalation
options.b: Hierarchical escalation, then hierarchical escalation
options.c: Hierarchical escalation, then functional escalation
options.d: Functional escalation, then functional escalation

questions.answer_text: Functional escalation, then hierarchical escalation
questions.explanation: Passing to a team with specialist skills is functional; passing to higher authority is hierarchical.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which stage of the incident management lifecycle MOST appropriately comes immediately before closure?

options.a: Detecting and recording the incident in the ticketing system with relevant details
options.b: Classifying the incident by category and urgency and giving initial support to the user
options.c: Escalating the incident hierarchically to senior management for an approval decision
options.d: Confirming with the user that service is restored and the issue is genuinely resolved

questions.answer_text: Confirming with the user that service is restored and the issue is genuinely resolved
questions.explanation: Before closing, the service desk verifies resolution, documents it and records the status.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A fault in an integration module repeatedly knocks out the same customer portal, and the service desk restores service each time. Which discipline should investigate the underlying cause?

options.a: Request fulfilment
options.b: Change enablement only
options.c: Incident management
options.d: Problem management

questions.answer_text: Problem management
questions.explanation: Problem management addresses root causes of multiple incidents; incident management restores service.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which service desk KPI measures the percentage of incidents resolved at the first interaction without further escalation?

options.a: Escalation rate, the share of incidents passed beyond first-level support
options.b: First contact resolution rate, the share resolved at the first interaction without escalation
options.c: Mean time to resolve, the average time from logging an incident to its closure
options.d: SLA compliance rate, the share of incidents resolved within the agreed timeframe

questions.answer_text: First contact resolution rate, the share resolved at the first interaction without escalation
questions.explanation: First contact resolution counts incidents resolved during the first interaction.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: An IT team applies an urgent patch to close an active security threat, using an expedited approval process and documenting and reviewing it afterwards. Which type of change is this?

options.a: Retrospective project
options.b: Normal change
options.c: Standard change
options.d: Emergency change

questions.answer_text: Emergency change
questions.explanation: Emergency changes address critical issues quickly, with expedited approval and later review.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A Nigerian bank deploys a new transaction-processing release and prepares a way to revert to the previous version if failures rise. What is this safeguard called?

options.a: A service catalogue
options.b: A change calendar
options.c: A risk transfer clause
options.d: A rollback plan

questions.answer_text: A rollback plan
questions.explanation: A rollback plan restores the previous state if a change fails or degrades service.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A mobile banking firm sets a Recovery Point Objective of 24 hours. What does this imply?

options.a: The system must have 24 redundant servers so that a single failure cannot interrupt it
options.b: Services must be restored within 24 hours of a disruption to avoid regulatory breaches
options.c: Backups must be tested at least once every 24 hours to confirm they can be restored
options.d: Up to 24 hours of data could be lost after a disruption before service is restored

questions.answer_text: Up to 24 hours of data could be lost after a disruption before service is restored
questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time; RTO is the maximum acceptable downtime.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which statement BEST contrasts business continuity planning (BCP) with IT disaster recovery (DR)?

options.a: BCP is broader, covering people, processes and operations, while DR is IT-centric and restores systems and data
options.b: BCP and DR are identical documents prepared by two different departments in an organisation
options.c: DR covers the whole organisation including premises, while BCP covers only servers and databases
options.d: BCP covers only cloud backups, while DR covers staff communication and crisis messaging

questions.answer_text: BCP is broader, covering people, processes and operations, while DR is IT-centric and restores systems and data
questions.explanation: DR is a technical component within the broader BCP.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which statement about onsite and cloud backups is MOST accurate?

options.a: Onsite backups restore quickly but can be lost to fire, flood or theft, so offsite or cloud copies are needed
options.b: Cloud backups cannot support NDPR compliance because data must always remain on premises
options.c: Onsite backups are immune to physical disasters, so no further copies are ever required
options.d: Cloud backups remove every data sovereignty concern because providers handle all compliance duties

questions.answer_text: Onsite backups restore quickly but can be lost to fire, flood or theft, so offsite or cloud copies are needed
questions.explanation: Onsite backups are fast but vulnerable to site-level events; cloud backups need provider and sovereignty checks.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: Which description matches the 3-2-1 backup rule?

options.a: Three system administrators, two firewalls and one VPN protecting the backup network
options.b: Three servers, two data centres and one cloud provider operating in an active configuration
options.c: Three monthly backups, two annual restoration tests and one external audit each year
options.d: Three copies of data, on two different media types, with one copy kept offsite

questions.answer_text: Three copies of data, on two different media types, with one copy kept offsite
questions.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule requires three copies, two media types and one offsite copy.

questions.module_title: IT Governance, Compliance, and Risk Management
questions.question: A hospital wants patient records to stay accessible if a primary server is compromised, using a secondary system that takes over automatically. Which mechanism is this?

options.a: Cold restoration
options.b: Change calendar
options.c: Data minimisation
options.d: Failover

questions.answer_text: Failover
questions.explanation: A failover system replaces the primary when it fails, keeping services available.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which of the following best describes IT operations in a digital business ecosystem?

options.a: A non-critical function in service delivery
options.b: A support function isolated from strategy
options.c: A strategic enabler of performance levels
options.d: A back-office role with business impact

questions.answer_text: A strategic enabler of performance levels
questions.explanation: In digital ecosystems IT operations underpin availability, scalability and compliance, so they enable performance strategically.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which ITSM framework emphasises continual service improvement and co-creation of value?

options.a: ITIL v4
options.b: COBIT Framework
options.d: MOF Model

questions.answer_text: ITIL v4
questions.explanation: ITIL v4 centres on the Service Value System, continual improvement and value co-creation.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Operational Level Agreements (OLAs) are internal agreements between:

options.a: Auditors and security officers
options.b: Users and the helpdesk
options.c: Customers and service providers
options.d: Internal service support groups

questions.answer_text: Internal service support groups
questions.explanation: OLAs define commitments between internal support groups so the external SLA can be met; SLAs are with customers.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A hybrid project methodology is:

options.a: Combine hybrid practices
options.b: Integrate manual methods
options.c: Apply AI planning
options.d: Use outdated tools

questions.answer_text: Combine hybrid practices
questions.explanation: A hybrid methodology blends elements of different approaches, typically predictive (Waterfall) and adaptive (Agile) practices.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which pairing correctly classifies strategic and operational IT activities?

options.a: Both are strategic activities when they are performed by the Chief Information Officer
options.b: Evaluating emerging technologies for a five-year plan is strategic; monitoring uptime and patching are operational
options.c: Applying patches is strategic, while selecting the five-year technology direction is operational
options.d: Both are operational activities when they are performed within a regulated bank

questions.answer_text: Evaluating emerging technologies for a five-year plan is strategic; monitoring uptime and patching are operational
questions.explanation: Strategic IT is future-oriented and exploratory; operational IT is current and execution-focused.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a defining feature of a digital business ecosystem?

options.a: Rigid, closed supply chains with no shared platforms or interfaces between participants
options.b: Platform-based interaction in which participants produce, exchange and consume value in real time
options.c: Connectivity between participants through shared infrastructures, data platforms and APIs
options.d: Openness and interoperability that let systems from different organisations work together

questions.answer_text: Rigid, closed supply chains with no shared platforms or interfaces between participants
questions.explanation: Ecosystems are characterised by connectivity, openness, interoperability and platform-based interaction rather than rigid closed chains.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: During a flash sale, an e-commerce platform's infrastructure automatically expands and contracts without performance degradation. Which IT operations responsibility does this show?

options.a: Maintaining legacy mainframe batch processing
options.b: Managing scalability and elasticity
options.c: Enforcing manual change approvals
options.d: Reducing the number of supported platforms

questions.answer_text: Managing scalability and elasticity
questions.explanation: Elastic infrastructure scales horizontally or vertically with demand.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: IT operations implement audit trails, access logs, encryption and compliance reporting that can withstand legal scrutiny. Which contribution of operations is this?

options.a: Supporting regulatory compliance and data governance through verifiable controls and evidence
options.b: Marketing digital services to customers through personalised campaigns and promotions
options.c: Reducing headcount by automating routine administrative tasks within the IT department
options.d: Developing new digital products and features for customers in competitive markets

questions.answer_text: Supporting regulatory compliance and data governance through verifiable controls and evidence
questions.explanation: Operations teams embed controls and evidence required by regulations such as GDPR and the NDPR.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: An ITSM approach moves a bank from reactive firefighting and a tools-focused view to proactive problem management and defining value in terms of services delivered. Which shift is this?

options.a: From technology-centric administration to a proactive, service-oriented, process-based discipline
options.b: From service management to hardware procurement and asset leasing across departments
options.c: From IT governance to project management delivered through short iterative sprints
options.d: From centralised to decentralised data centres operated by independent business units

questions.answer_text: From technology-centric administration to a proactive, service-oriented, process-based discipline
questions.explanation: ITSM defines value through services and introduces proactive measures instead of reacting.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which organisation would the course MOST likely recommend to adopt ISO/IEC 20000?

options.a: A regulated bank or telecom seeking certification to demonstrate ITSM maturity and auditability
options.b: A tiny retailer with a single laptop that has no formal service processes or support staff
options.c: A start-up that wants no documentation and prefers informal, undocumented support routines
options.d: A school with no IT assets that outsources all of its administrative functions to parents

questions.answer_text: A regulated bank or telecom seeking certification to demonstrate ITSM maturity and auditability
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 20000 is a certifiable standard suited to regulated sectors where compliance and auditability matter.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A small Nigerian firm that runs mainly Microsoft technologies wants a simple, cost-effective ITSM approach. Which framework fits BEST?

options.a: Microsoft Operations Framework (MOF), a lightweight ITSM framework for Microsoft-centric SMEs
options.b: ITIL 4 at full scale, with all practices and extensive staff certification
options.c: COBIT 2019 full implementation, an enterprise-wide governance and management system
options.d: ISO/IEC 27001, an information security management system standard for certification

questions.answer_text: Microsoft Operations Framework (MOF), a lightweight ITSM framework for Microsoft-centric SMEs
questions.explanation: MOF is a lightweight framework for Microsoft-centric SMEs, though less comprehensive than ITIL.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Within the ITIL service lifecycle, to which stage do incident management and request fulfilment BELONG?

options.a: Service Strategy
options.b: Service Operation
options.c: Service Design
options.d: Continual Service Improvement

questions.answer_text: Service Operation
questions.explanation: Incident management, problem management and request fulfilment are Service Operation processes.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A telecom defines Service Level Agreements, availability targets and security requirements before launching a new service. Which ITIL stage is this?

options.a: Service Transition
options.b: Service Design
options.c: Service Strategy
options.d: Service Operation

questions.answer_text: Service Design
questions.explanation: Service Design creates reliable, scalable services and defines SLAs and security requirements.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Incident trend data from live operations feeds back into portfolio decisions and improvement initiatives. Which feature of the ITIL service lifecycle does this show?

options.a: It is cyclical and integrated, so Service Operation insights inform Strategy and Improvement
options.b: It is limited to documentation produced in the Service Strategy stage only
options.c: It is strictly linear, so each stage is completed and never informs the others
options.d: It operates only after incidents end and is used for billing customers

questions.answer_text: It is cyclical and integrated, so Service Operation insights inform Strategy and Improvement
questions.explanation: The lifecycle is a cyclical, integrated system in which operations insights shape strategy and improvement.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: MTN's network team has an internal commitment to restore connectivity within two hours, supporting the customer-facing SLA. Which statement BEST describes the relationship?

options.a: The OLA is a customer contract that replaces the SLA once the service is live
options.b: The OLA is a vendor contract that is unrelated to the targets in the SLA
options.c: The OLA aligns internal support group commitments to the SLA target, giving end-to-end accountability
options.d: The OLA and SLA both exist only between auditors and information security officers

questions.answer_text: The OLA aligns internal support group commitments to the SLA target, giving end-to-end accountability
questions.explanation: OLAs are internal agreements that underpin external SLAs.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which element is NOT normally a component of a well-formed SLA?

options.a: Escalation procedures and penalties for missed targets
options.b: A guaranteed profit margin for the customer
options.c: Service description and scope of the service provided
options.d: Measurable performance metrics such as availability and response time

questions.answer_text: A guaranteed profit margin for the customer
questions.explanation: SLAs specify the service, metrics, responsibilities, penalties and escalation; they do not guarantee customer profit.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which sequence BEST matches the ITIL v4 style change lifecycle described in the course?

options.a: Review, implement, assess, approve and then request the change formally
options.b: Test, implement, request, close and then approve the change retrospectively
options.c: Implement, approve, request, review and test the change in the live environment
options.d: Request, assess risk and impact, approve through the CAB, test, implement and review

questions.answer_text: Request, assess risk and impact, approve through the CAB, test, implement and review
questions.explanation: Changes are requested, assessed, authorised, tested, implemented in production and reviewed.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Leaders of a bank form a guiding coalition and communicate a vision after creating urgency for a digital banking upgrade. Which change model are they following?

options.a: The McKinsey 7-S framework, which aligns seven organisational elements
options.b: The ADKAR model, which focuses on individual awareness, desire and ability
options.c: Kotter's 8-step model, which begins with urgency and a guiding coalition
options.d: Lewin's three-stage model of unfreezing, changing and refreezing

questions.answer_text: Kotter's 8-step model, which begins with urgency and a guiding coalition
questions.explanation: Creating urgency, building a guiding coalition and communicating a vision are early Kotter steps.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A university trains staff and explains the reason for a new student portal before launch to prepare people for the change. In Lewin's model, this is the stage of:

options.a: Change
options.b: Reinforce
options.c: Unfreeze
options.d: Refreeze

questions.answer_text: Unfreeze
questions.explanation: Preparing people and building readiness before the change is the unfreezing stage.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Employees understand why a new ERP is needed and what is expected but show no personal willingness to participate. Which ADKAR element is MISSING?

options.a: Knowledge
options.b: Awareness
options.c: Reinforcement
options.d: Desire

questions.answer_text: Desire
questions.explanation: Awareness is present; the missing step is Desire, the willingness to support and take part in the change.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Bank tellers resist a new teller system because they fear job loss. Which response is MOST consistent with the course's resistance strategies?

options.a: Delay all communication about the new system until after go-live is complete
options.b: Disable the old system on the go-live date to force adoption without explanation
options.c: Engage and communicate with stakeholders, offer training and address their concerns
options.d: Hire additional tellers to replace those who object to the new system

questions.answer_text: Engage and communicate with stakeholders, offer training and address their concerns
questions.explanation: Resistance driven by fear is handled through engagement, communication, training and support.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A university IT helpdesk offers tailored support for students with disabilities. Which SERVQUAL dimension does this reflect?

options.a: Reliability
options.b: Empathy
options.c: Assurance
options.d: Tangibles

questions.answer_text: Empathy
questions.explanation: Empathy means individualised care and attention to customers' particular needs.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: An SLA guarantees 99.99% annual availability. Approximately how much downtime does that permit per year?

options.a: About 4.4 hours
options.b: About 3.7 days
options.c: About 52 minutes
options.d: About 8.8 hours

questions.answer_text: About 52 minutes
questions.explanation: 0.01% of 525,600 minutes is about 52.6 minutes; 99.9% gives about 8.8 hours.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A team reduces Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) from four hours to one hour but Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) is unchanged. What does this show?

options.a: Failures occur less often, and each one is repaired at the same speed as before
options.b: Availability has decreased because repairs are now completed in less time
options.c: Failures occur just as often, but service is restored much faster
options.d: The system has become more reliable because it now fails far less frequently

questions.answer_text: Failures occur just as often, but service is restored much faster
questions.explanation: MTTR measures repair speed; MTBF measures how long a system runs between failures.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A project's requirements keep expanding after approval without matching changes to time or budget. What is this risk called?

options.a: Technical debt
options.b: Resource levelling
options.c: Scope creep
options.d: Vendor lock-in

questions.answer_text: Scope creep
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled expansion of project scope is scope creep.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which project is MOST suitable for the Waterfall methodology?

options.a: A start-up app with evolving requirements that depends on early market feedback
options.b: An innovation project in which speed and adaptability are crucial to success
options.c: A government system upgrade with well-defined, stable requirements and heavy documentation needs
options.d: A mobile product with rapidly changing requirements under continuous delivery

questions.answer_text: A government system upgrade with well-defined, stable requirements and heavy documentation needs
questions.explanation: Waterfall suits fixed scope and well-understood requirements; Agile suits evolving ones.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: In Scrum, which role owns and prioritises the Product Backlog, and which role removes impediments?

options.a: The sponsor owns the backlog; the auditor removes impediments
options.b: The Product Owner owns the backlog; the Scrum Master removes impediments
options.c: The Scrum Master owns the backlog; the Product Owner removes impediments
options.d: The Development Team owns the backlog; the Product Owner facilitates meetings

questions.answer_text: The Product Owner owns the backlog; the Scrum Master removes impediments
questions.explanation: The Product Owner represents the customer and prioritises the backlog; the Scrum Master facilitates and removes obstacles.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A public sector IT procurement needs formal stage-wise planning, defined roles and strict governance. Which methodology is MOST suitable?

options.a: Ad hoc project delivery
options.b: Pure Scrum
options.c: Kanban without governance
options.d: PRINCE2

questions.answer_text: PRINCE2
questions.explanation: PRINCE2 is process-based with defined roles and stage-wise reviews, useful for public sector compliance.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A bank plans a formal Waterfall procurement and deployment but delivers its mobile app features in short Agile sprints. Which approach is this?

options.a: A pure Waterfall model with fixed phases and no iterative delivery
options.b: A hybrid methodology combining predictive and adaptive practices
options.c: A pure Scrum model with sprints and no formal governance stages
options.d: A Business Process Reengineering initiative that redesigns the whole organisation

questions.answer_text: A hybrid methodology combining predictive and adaptive practices
questions.explanation: Hybrid approaches blend Waterfall governance with Agile flexibility.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A project has a Planned Value of 200,000, an Earned Value of 150,000 and an Actual Cost of 180,000. Which conclusion is CORRECT?

options.a: CPI is 1.2, so it is under budget; SPI is 1.33, so it is ahead of schedule
options.b: CPI is 1.0 and SPI is 1.0, so the project is exactly on plan
options.c: CPI is 0.83, so it is under budget; SPI is 0.75, so it is ahead of schedule
options.d: CPI is about 0.83, so it is over budget; SPI is 0.75, so it is behind schedule

questions.answer_text: CPI is about 0.83, so it is over budget; SPI is 0.75, so it is behind schedule
questions.explanation: CPI equals EV divided by AC (150/180 = 0.83) and SPI equals EV divided by PV (150/200 = 0.75); both below 1 mean over budget and behind schedule.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: Which governance mechanism BEST controls scope and approves major changes in a public sector IT project?

options.a: Removing documentation to speed delivery
options.b: Verbal approvals from the vendor
options.c: Informal agreements between developers
options.d: A steering committee with formal change control

questions.answer_text: A steering committee with formal change control
questions.explanation: Steering committees and change control provide oversight, transparency and accountability.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A bank phases the deployment of a new core system across cities and uses change management and asset tracking to avoid network disruption. Which ITIL lifecycle stage is MOST directly involved?

options.a: Service Strategy
options.b: Service Design
options.c: Service Operation
options.d: Service Transition

questions.answer_text: Service Transition
questions.explanation: Service Transition covers change management, release and deployment and asset and configuration control.

questions.module_title: IT Operations, Service, and Change Management
questions.question: A cloud-hosted service is deliberately built so it can be moved easily between hosting platforms. Which ISO 9126-based quality characteristic does this MOST directly reflect?

options.a: Reliability
options.b: Maintainability
options.c: Usability
options.d: Portability

questions.answer_text: Portability
questions.explanation: Portability is the ability of a service to adapt to different platforms, while maintainability concerns ease of modification.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Concurrently, infrastructure leaders at Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (HPE) implemented dashboards tracking uptime, customer response delays, and service reliability metrics. The fundamental managerial objective guiding this initiative centres on:

options.a: Outsourcing infrastructure accountability to external cloud vendors entirely
options.b: Measuring operational efficiency and business impact using defined indicators
options.c: Eliminating governance oversight through decentralised reporting mechanisms
options.d: Expanding organisational hierarchy through additional supervisory departments

questions.answer_text: Measuring operational efficiency and business impact using defined indicators
questions.explanation: Uptime, response delay and reliability dashboards are defined indicators used to measure efficiency and business impact.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: After cloud cost overruns affected operational budgets at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited, governance teams introduced dashboards tracking system uptime, customer complaints, and deployment delays. Which principle is being implemented MOST directly?

options.a: Infrastructure governance through centralised database administration controls
options.b: Performance measurement through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) analysis
options.c: Strategic alignment through enterprise digital transformation initiatives
options.d: Resource optimisation through hybrid workforce restructuring initiatives

questions.answer_text: Performance measurement through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) analysis
questions.explanation: Tracking uptime, complaints and delays against defined indicators is KPI-based performance measurement.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: During enterprise continuity assessments at Siemens Digital Industries Software Division, reviewers identified inadequate backup systems across mission-critical operations. Management responded by investing in resilient disaster recovery infrastructure. This decision primarily supports:

options.a: Strategic outsourcing through dependence on external service providers
options.b: Business continuity through proactive mitigation of operational disruption risks
options.c: Organisational decentralisation through autonomous regional infrastructure units
options.d: Workforce governance through employee performance monitoring initiatives

questions.answer_text: Business continuity through proactive mitigation of operational disruption risks
questions.explanation: Resilient DR infrastructure protects mission-critical operations from disruption, which is business continuity.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Following a ransomware disruption affecting customer databases at Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), the IT recovery team invoked the disaster recovery plan. Which governance action should be prioritised immediately after restoring core transaction systems?

options.a: Restore from the most recent backup without verifying backup integrity
options.b: Disable all firewall rules to accelerate remaining data restoration
options.c: Conduct a forensic investigation to determine root cause and data exfiltration scope
options.d: Schedule a post-incident review for the next fiscal year

questions.answer_text: Conduct a forensic investigation to determine root cause and data exfiltration scope
questions.explanation: After restoration, a forensic investigation establishes root cause and whether data left the organisation, which drives notification and remediation.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: An e-learning platform tracks server CPU load but not availability during examination periods, when thousands of students log in. Which KPI design principle has been neglected?

options.a: Frequent revision of KPIs to reflect technological and market changes
options.b: Benchmarking of results against industry standards and peer organisations
options.c: Granularity of metrics, with separate indicators for each individual service
options.d: Alignment of KPIs with business priorities such as availability during exams

questions.answer_text: Alignment of KPIs with business priorities such as availability during exams
questions.explanation: KPIs must reflect business priorities such as uptime during exams, not only technical measures.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: A CIO replaces one combined "application uptime" KPI with separate KPIs for email and the ERP system. Which KPI design principle is applied?

options.a: Benchmarking
options.b: Automation
options.c: Granularity
options.d: Alignment

questions.answer_text: Granularity
questions.explanation: Breaking metrics down by service makes KPIs specific to each service's performance needs.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which IT measure belongs to the Learning and Growth perspective of an IT Balanced Scorecard?

options.a: Net Promoter Score gathered from customers using the platform
options.b: Mean time to resolve incidents raised by users of the platform
options.c: Percentage of staff certified in new cloud technologies
options.d: Cost per transaction on the payments platform for the financial year

questions.answer_text: Percentage of staff certified in new cloud technologies
questions.explanation: Learning and Growth covers capabilities such as skills, training and innovation.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which IT measure belongs to the Internal Processes perspective of the Balanced Scorecard?

options.a: Customer satisfaction survey scores gathered after each transaction
options.b: Mean time to resolve incidents and SLA adherence
options.c: Revenue growth from digital channels over the financial year
options.d: Hours of staff training completed on emerging technologies

questions.question: An organisation wants a governance-linked framework that includes metrics such as IT goal achievement rate and compliance. Which is MOST suitable?

questions.question: A call centre automates ticket handling to lower cost per ticket dramatically, but user satisfaction falls. Which statement BEST explains the situation?

questions.question: An IT department needs real-time visualisation of machine and log data across its infrastructure. Which tool category and example BEST fit?

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which three core phases make up the business continuity planning lifecycle in the course?

questions.explanation: BCP begins with assessing risks, analysing business impact and developing continuity strategies.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: An online examination platform sets an RTO of one hour and an RPO of five minutes. Which interpretation is CORRECT?

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which statement about ISO 22301 and NIST SP 800-34 is MOST accurate?

options.a: NIST SP 800-34 is certifiable worldwide, while ISO 22301 is only a US-centric guideline

options.d: ISO 22301 is a certifiable global continuity management standard, while NIST SP 800-34 is a US-centric contingency planning guideline

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: A bank's core banking system cannot tolerate more than minutes of downtime. Which disaster recovery site type is MOST appropriate?

questions.explanation: Hot sites are fully equipped and synchronised for near-instant failover, at higher cost.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: A Nigerian SME with a limited budget can tolerate days of downtime after a major disaster. Which DR site is the MOST cost-appropriate?

options.a: Mirrored active-active site
options.b: Hot site
options.c: Cold site
options.d: Dedicated multi-region failover

questions.answer_text: Cold site
questions.explanation: Cold sites are low-cost with slow recovery (days to weeks) and no pre-installed equipment.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which description fits a warm disaster recovery site?

options.d: An empty room with power and network links but no equipment or data

questions.answer_text: Pre-installed hardware with periodic data updates, giving moderate recovery time and cost
questions.explanation: A warm site sits between cold and hot, with equipment ready and data refreshed periodically.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which DR test provides the GREATEST assurance, although it is the most disruptive?

options.a: A walkthrough that talks stakeholders through the recovery steps

options.d: A simulation that replicates a disaster scenario such as server failure

questions.answer_text: A full failover test that switches operations to the DR site
questions.explanation: A full failover test actually switches operations to the DR site, validating the plan end to end.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which ordering of DR testing methods runs from least to most realistic?

options.a: Walkthrough, full failover, checklist review, simulation
options.b: Simulation, checklist review, full failover, walkthrough
options.c: Full failover, simulation, walkthrough, checklist review
options.d: Checklist review, walkthrough, simulation, full failover

questions.explanation: Testing progresses from document checks to rehearsal to scenario simulation to full failover.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which feature of DR tools such as Veeam, Acronis and AWS DR MOST directly reduces recovery time and human error?

options.a: Printed recovery checklists stored in the server room
options.b: Automation of backup scheduling, replication and failover
options.c: Quarterly staff meetings that review the continuity strategy

questions.explanation: Automation streamlines recovery and reduces mean time to recover.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: How does resilience engineering differ from traditional risk management?

options.a: It relies on a single large backup site to restore services after any outage
options.b: It assumes failures can be fully prevented, so it concentrates on perimeter controls
options.c: It designs systems to withstand, adapt to and recover from disruption, not only prevent failures
options.d: It addresses only natural disasters and excludes cyberattacks and human error

questions.answer_text: It designs systems to withstand, adapt to and recover from disruption, not only prevent failures
questions.explanation: Resilience engineering assumes disruptions will occur and builds capacity to absorb and recover from them.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which pairing correctly classifies resilience strategies?

options.c: Chaos engineering is reactive; failover to a hot site after an outage is proactive
options.d: Both are purely reactive because they follow a failure of some kind

questions.answer_text: Chaos engineering is proactive; failover to a hot site after an outage is reactive
questions.explanation: Chaos engineering anticipates and tests failures in advance, whereas failover responds after a disruption.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: In Netflix's Simian Army, what does Chaos Monkey do?

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: A cloud team wants to test whether its service survives the loss of an entire data centre or availability zone. Which Simian Army tool simulates this?

options.a: Chaos Gorilla

options.c: Latency Monkey

questions.explanation: Chaos Gorilla simulates entire zone or data centre outages.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Which statement about Basel III and SWIFT requirements for the financial sector is MOST accurate?

questions.answer_text: They drive resilience, risk management, continuity and high-availability requirements that regulators such as the CBN align with
questions.explanation: Basel III and SWIFT frameworks underpin resilience expectations for banks and payment systems.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: A tabletop exercise simulating a DDoS attack on a payment platform reveals a three-hour RTO gap, and the firm responds by enhancing load balancing. Which BEST describes the value of tabletop exercises?

options.a: They replace the need for backups, failover sites and recovery testing
options.b: They are used only after incidents to assign responsibility for failures

questions.answer_text: They expose weaknesses in plans and communication before a real incident occurs
questions.explanation: Structured simulations identify gaps such as RTO shortfalls so they can be fixed in advance.

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT
questions.question: Google's Gmail remains available when a single data centre fails because workloads are offset by global redundancy. Which resilience concept does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: Manual failover, where engineers redirect traffic after users complain

questions.module_title: Performance, Continuity, and Resilience in IT

questions.answer_text: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)
questions.explanation: Longer MTBF indicates failures are being prevented or occurring less frequently.

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

options.d: It means replacing every paper form with a PDF version across departments

questions.answer_text: It uses digital technologies to fundamentally change operations and value delivery, requiring leadership, skills and culture

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT
questions.question: A property registry uses blockchain-based records to streamline title verification and reduce fraud. Which statement about blockchain is CORRECT?

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT
questions.question: Which application of AI in finance and IT management does the course describe?

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT
questions.question: A firm shifts from purchasing servers to subscribing to cloud services. Which financial implication is MOST accurate?

questions.question: Which statement about Industry 4.0 is MOST accurate?

options.b: The first industrial revolution, marked by steam power and mechanised production

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.question: A company buys data-centre hardware and licences, which are depreciated over time, and also pays monthly cloud fees and maintenance contracts. How should these be classified?

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.question: A steering group asks, "Are we working on the right projects, aligned to strategy?" Which approach does this question MOST reflect?

options.b: Waterfall execution focused on sequential delivery stages

questions.explanation: Portfolio management evaluates the whole set of projects against strategy and constraints.

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT

questions.module_title: Emerging Trends and Financial Management in IT
