questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Executives at a Lagos retail chain describe their upgrade of point-of-sale terminals as "digital transformation." Which observation BEST challenges that description?

options.a: Transformation is defined by how many software licences the firm purchases in a financial year
options.b: Transformation rethinks business models, processes and customer value, not just the adoption of new tools
options.c: Transformation applies only to firms that already operate cloud-native platforms
options.d: Transformation is achieved once every paper process has been replaced with an email workflow

questions.answer_text: Transformation rethinks business models, processes and customer value, not just the adoption of new tools
questions.explanation: Digital transformation is a profound change in how an organisation operates and delivers value, not merely technology adoption.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which statement BEST captures the relationship between innovation and digital transformation?

options.a: Innovation and transformation are unrelated, since innovation requires no technology
options.b: Innovation concerns only product design, while transformation concerns only infrastructure
options.c: Innovation is a by-product of transformation and has no influence on strategy
options.d: Innovation is the engine that ensures technology is applied creatively to meet real needs and create value

questions.answer_text: Innovation is the engine that ensures technology is applied creatively to meet real needs and create value
questions.explanation: Digital transformation thrives on innovation; creative application of technology creates new markets, efficiency and competitiveness.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Netflix shifted from DVD rentals to cloud streaming, used big data and AI for personalised recommendations, and invested in original content. Which lesson is MOST supported?

options.a: Streaming succeeded mainly because DVD rental stores closed for regulatory reasons in major markets
options.b: Proactive transformation combined with continuous investment in technology and content can disrupt an industry
options.c: Personalised recommendations matter only for companies that operate physical retail outlets
options.d: Original content is unnecessary if the recommendation algorithm is accurate enough to retain users

questions.answer_text: Proactive transformation combined with continuous investment in technology and content can disrupt an industry
questions.explanation: The case shows proactive business model change, data use and sustained investment enabling disruption of traditional media.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Kodak invented the digital camera in 1975 but shelved it to protect its film business. What does this case BEST illustrate?

options.a: Competitors Canon and Nikon succeeded only through lower pricing
options.b: Digital cameras were technically inferior and therefore unprofitable for early adopters
options.c: Film businesses cannot transform because their assets are too specialised
options.d: Reluctance to disrupt a profitable existing model can cause decline even for an industry pioneer

questions.answer_text: Reluctance to disrupt a profitable existing model can cause decline even for an industry pioneer
questions.explanation: Kodak's complacency and protection of its film model let competitors capture the digital market.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Blockbuster failed to respond when Netflix moved video rental online. Which interpretation is MOST consistent with the course?

options.a: The collapse shows how incumbents tied to legacy models are disrupted by digital business models
options.b: Blockbuster collapsed because streaming content was cheaper to produce than physical DVD stock
options.c: Netflix succeeded solely by acquiring the customer database of the established rental chain
options.d: Blockbuster lacked enough physical stores in key locations to compete with the new entrant

questions.answer_text: The collapse shows how incumbents tied to legacy models are disrupted by digital business models
questions.explanation: Failing to adapt to streaming allowed a digital disruptor to redefine the industry.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A bank defines its digital vision, roadmap and governance, but has no clear owner for resource allocation or change management. Which transformation layer is weakest?

options.a: Technology layer, which comprises cloud, AI, IoT and cybersecurity tools
options.b: Strategic layer, which provides leadership and direction on why and where to transform
options.c: Infrastructure layer, which supports hybrid cloud and virtualised environments
options.d: Customer layer, which focuses on the end-user experience of digital services

questions.answer_text: Strategic layer, which provides leadership and direction on why and where to transform
questions.explanation: The strategic layer covers vision, strategy, governance and change management that guide digital efforts.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A firm installs modern workflow software but keeps outdated approval routes and manual hand-offs, creating bottlenecks. Which layer needs attention?

options.a: Technology layer, through additional cloud subscriptions and newer analytics software licences
options.b: Data and integration layer, through master data management and API-based system connections
options.c: Business process layer, through process reengineering and lean, agile operations
options.d: Strategic layer, through a revised vision statement and a refreshed digital roadmap document

questions.answer_text: Business process layer, through process reengineering and lean, agile operations
questions.explanation: Even with new technology, outdated processes constrain innovation; the business process layer redesigns workflows.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Two systems in a firm hold conflicting customer records and cannot exchange data, so decisions are flawed. Which layer is MOST directly implicated?

options.a: Business process layer, which maps customer journeys and removes workflow bottlenecks
options.b: Data and integration layer, which ensures data flows smoothly and securely across systems
options.c: Customer layer, which captures end-user feedback and redesigns the customer-facing experience
options.d: Strategic layer, which sets the digital vision and the allocation of transformation resources

questions.answer_text: Data and integration layer, which ensures data flows smoothly and securely across systems
questions.explanation: Data governance, APIs, microservices and master data management belong to the data and integration layer.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which element would a transformation team place in the TECHNOLOGY layer?

options.a: Cloud computing, AI and analytics, IoT, blockchain, RPA, mobile and cybersecurity tools
options.b: Hybrid infrastructure policies covering on-premise servers, virtualisation and containers
options.c: Customer journey maps and end-to-end experience redesign across every customer touchpoint
options.d: Vision statements, executive sponsorship, governance and the digital roadmap that guides priorities

questions.answer_text: Cloud computing, AI and analytics, IoT, blockchain, RPA, mobile and cybersecurity tools
questions.explanation: The technology layer comprises tools and platforms that power digital initiatives.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.topic: Role of IT in business models
questions.question: A cloud-based service lets a company scale capacity up and down without investing heavily in physical infrastructure. Which shift in business model does this MOST directly enable?

options.a: From data-driven to intuition-driven decision-making led by the most senior managers
options.b: From customer-centred to product-centred operations built around physical stores and stock
options.c: From fixed, asset-heavy models to flexible, subscription or on-demand digital models
options.d: From digital back to paper-based processes in order to reduce exposure to technology risk

questions.answer_text: From fixed, asset-heavy models to flexible, subscription or on-demand digital models
questions.explanation: Cloud computing, big data and platforms enable digital business models without large physical investment.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A board treats IT purely as a cost centre and funds projects in isolation, leading to technical debt, duplication and failed initiatives. What is the MOST appropriate conclusion?

options.a: IT spending should be reduced further until each project proves its return independently
options.b: Duplication is best resolved by letting each department select and fund its own tools
options.c: Technical debt is unavoidable and bears no relationship to governance or investment choices
options.d: IT must be treated as a core business asset with strategic alignment, governance and long-term investment

questions.answer_text: IT must be treated as a core business asset with strategic alignment, governance and long-term investment
questions.explanation: Long-term IT investment succeeds when it is strategically aligned and governed, not treated as a cost.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Moniepoint scaled across Nigeria through an agent management system, cloud infrastructure, data analytics, POS and app optimisation for low-bandwidth use, and fraud prevention. What does this case BEST demonstrate?

options.a: Targeted IT investments aligned to underserved customers can drive rapid scale and trust
options.b: Low-bandwidth optimisation is relevant only in rural areas without any smartphones
options.c: Fintechs succeed only when they open large networks of physical bank branches
options.d: Cybersecurity spending is unnecessary where agents handle transactions in person

questions.answer_text: Targeted IT investments aligned to underserved customers can drive rapid scale and trust
questions.explanation: Aligned investments in agents, cloud, analytics, accessibility and security allowed rapid scale and trust.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which Moniepoint IT investment BEST addresses the challenge of unreliable connectivity and low-end devices?

options.a: Cybersecurity and fraud prevention systems that build trust
options.b: Data analytics tools identifying transaction patterns and agent performance
options.c: Cloud infrastructure that scales services without physical branches
options.d: Mobile app and POS optimisation for low-bandwidth environments and low-end devices

questions.answer_text: Mobile app and POS optimisation for low-bandwidth environments and low-end devices
questions.explanation: Optimising apps and POS for low bandwidth directly addresses connectivity and device constraints.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A farmer uses soil-moisture sensors and weather data to schedule irrigation automatically. Which emerging technology category is MOST directly involved?

options.a: Virtual reality, simulating immersive environments for training and visualisation
options.b: Blockchain, providing a decentralised and tamper-resistant ledger for digital identity
options.c: Internet of Things (IoT), connecting devices that collect and exchange data
options.d: Quantum computing, solving complex cryptographic and pharmaceutical research problems

questions.answer_text: Internet of Things (IoT), connecting devices that collect and exchange data
questions.explanation: IoT-enabled devices monitor conditions and enable data collection and automation in agriculture.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which description of machine learning is MOST accurate?

options.a: A mobile network technology that delivers high-speed connectivity to remote locations
options.b: A subset of AI that learns from data to improve its performance without explicit programming for each task
options.c: A decentralised ledger that records transactions across many participating computers
options.d: A hardware standard that connects physical sensors to cloud servers over mobile networks

questions.answer_text: A subset of AI that learns from data to improve its performance without explicit programming for each task
questions.explanation: Machine learning is a subset of AI that learns patterns from data, used in fraud detection and recommendations.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A fintech wants a tamper-resistant shared record for digital identity and financial services. Which technology is MOST suitable?

options.a: 5G connectivity
options.b: Blockchain
options.c: Robotic process automation
options.d: Augmented reality

questions.answer_text: Blockchain
questions.explanation: Blockchain provides a decentralised, tamper-resistant ledger used in digital identity and financial services.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: In healthcare, an AI system helps diagnose disease from scans and a hospital offers telemedicine consultations. Which statement is MOST accurate?

options.a: Telemedicine is feasible only where users have unlimited high-speed bandwidth at all times
options.b: Emerging technologies improve diagnostics and access to care by transforming how services are delivered
options.c: Healthcare is largely unaffected by digitalisation because of its strict regulation
options.d: AI in healthcare only automates billing and cannot support clinical decisions or diagnosis

questions.answer_text: Emerging technologies improve diagnostics and access to care by transforming how services are delivered
questions.explanation: AI and telemedicine are examples of emerging technologies reshaping healthcare delivery.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which outcome BEST demonstrates an agile IT infrastructure?

options.a: The company keeps all servers on premises so that it never depends on outside vendors
options.b: The company can respond quickly to customer needs, scale services and launch products faster than competitors
options.c: The company freezes its technology choices for five years in order to control spending
options.d: The company standardises on one legacy system to reduce training and support costs

questions.answer_text: The company can respond quickly to customer needs, scale services and launch products faster than competitors
questions.explanation: Agile infrastructure lets a firm adapt, scale and innovate rapidly.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which statement BEST describes strategic alignment of IT and business?

options.a: Allocating the IT budget in equal shares across every business unit in the organisation
options.b: Ensuring IT has its own separate strategy that is developed independently of the business plan
options.c: Harmonising IT strategy and capabilities with business goals so technology supports market share, innovation and growth
options.d: Selecting technology according to whatever competitors in the sector currently happen to use

questions.answer_text: Harmonising IT strategy and capabilities with business goals so technology supports market share, innovation and growth
questions.explanation: Strategic alignment synchronises IT and business objectives so IT is a source of sustained competitive advantage.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A firm adopts AI, IoT or blockchain early, ahead of rivals. Under the course's view of IT investment as a competitive advantage, what is the MOST likely benefit?

options.a: Freedom from sector regulation because early adopters are treated as innovation pilots
options.b: Elimination of employee training needs because new technologies are intuitive to use
options.c: Positioning for new business models and a culture of continuous innovation
options.d: Guaranteed lower costs than all competitors in the short term, with no further investment needed

questions.answer_text: Positioning for new business models and a culture of continuous innovation
questions.explanation: Early adoption can position a company for new models and foster continuous innovation, if managed well.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A company has strong technology but employees avoid the new systems and managers resist changes to their routines. Which challenge is MOST evident?

options.a: Regulatory uncertainty about data localisation and overlapping compliance directives
options.b: Resistance to change, which must be addressed through leadership, communication and training
options.c: Vendor lock-in resulting from dependence on proprietary APIs and platform contracts
options.d: Infrastructure instability caused by unreliable electricity and inconsistent network coverage

questions.answer_text: Resistance to change, which must be addressed through leadership, communication and training
questions.explanation: Reluctance to adopt new systems is a primary human challenge of digital transformation.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A bank lacks staff who can manage AI and cloud platforms. Which solution is MOST aligned with the course?

options.a: Prioritise upskilling and training programmes and form partnerships with training institutions
options.b: Reduce reliance on advanced technology so that training needs are avoided entirely
options.c: Outsource strategic decisions to the technology vendor on a permanent basis
options.d: Delay all digital projects until suitable skills appear naturally in the wider labour market

questions.answer_text: Prioritise upskilling and training programmes and form partnerships with training institutions
questions.explanation: The skills gap is addressed through upskilling, training programmes and partnerships.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A start-up must handle personal data in a regulated industry. Which challenge and response pair is MOST appropriate?

options.a: Cybersecurity and compliance, addressed through strong security controls and privacy-regulation compliance
options.b: Resistance to change, addressed through additional marketing campaigns to staff
options.c: Legacy integration, addressed by removing governance procedures that slow delivery
options.d: Skills gaps, addressed by reducing the number of digital services the start-up offers

questions.answer_text: Cybersecurity and compliance, addressed through strong security controls and privacy-regulation compliance
questions.explanation: Security and regulatory compliance are key digital transformation challenges requiring robust controls.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which combination lists challenges to innovation in Nigerian businesses identified in the course?

options.a: Surplus venture capital, no skills shortage and leadership that eagerly embraces change
options.b: Overly flexible regulation, fully reliable electricity and unlimited access to research partners
options.c: Excess skilled labour, abundant research funding, universal broadband and low resistance to change
options.d: Poor infrastructure and unreliable electricity, limited access to research, resistance to change and lack of technical expertise

questions.answer_text: Poor infrastructure and unreliable electricity, limited access to research, resistance to change and lack of technical expertise
questions.explanation: The course lists infrastructure, electricity, research access, resistance and expertise gaps as barriers.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Why should an organisation define success metrics before launching a digital transformation?

options.a: Metrics are needed for technology performance but not for customer or employee outcomes
options.b: Metrics should be chosen after results are known, to avoid bias in the evaluation
options.c: Without clear metrics, digital investments risk becoming costly experiments that cannot be justified
options.d: Metrics are required only for regulatory filing and have little management value

questions.answer_text: Without clear metrics, digital investments risk becoming costly experiments that cannot be justified
questions.explanation: Metrics demonstrate real improvement in performance, customer satisfaction, engagement and agility.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which set BEST reflects categories of metrics for measuring digital transformation success?

options.a: Business performance, customer experience, employee engagement and innovation capability
options.b: Server count, floor space, number of printers and the quantity of desk phones installed
options.c: Number of meetings held, email volume handled and total paper consumed each month
options.d: Staff headcount, office size and annual travel expenses of the executive team

questions.answer_text: Business performance, customer experience, employee engagement and innovation capability
questions.explanation: Success is reflected in tangible improvements in performance, customer satisfaction, employee engagement and agility.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Digital initiatives often fail not because technology is flawed but because:

options.a: Customers refuse to use digital channels in virtually all circumstances
options.b: Technology vendors always overcharge for support during the first year of implementation
options.c: Regulators prohibit automation in most industries so projects are halted early
options.d: Employees resist new systems and the organisation does not support the transition

questions.answer_text: Employees resist new systems and the organisation does not support the transition
questions.explanation: Change management addresses the human side where resistance and weak support cause failures.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which pair of tactics is MOST consistent with effective change management in digital programmes?

options.a: Pilot programmes to test changes and training and support to equip staff
options.b: Mandatory adoption announced by email with no feedback channels
options.c: Restricting information until after go-live to avoid anxiety
options.d: Rewarding speed of rollout regardless of user readiness

questions.answer_text: Pilot programmes to test changes and training and support to equip staff
questions.explanation: Pilots and training are core change management strategies, with communication and feedback.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A bank's IT infrastructure can scale during peak season, integrate new services via APIs and recover quickly from failure. Which combination of benefits does this show?

options.a: Centralised control and slower change that reduce exposure to market volatility
options.b: Agility, scalability and resilience that support innovation
options.c: Cost avoidance and regulatory exemption that remove the need for governance reviews
options.d: Reduced staffing and fewer customers because systems no longer need user support

questions.answer_text: Agility, scalability and resilience that support innovation
questions.explanation: Agile infrastructure enables responsiveness, scale and resilience that underpin innovation.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which action would BEST foster innovation in a Nigerian firm facing poor infrastructure and limited research access?

options.a: Centralising all ideas with the board and discouraging proposals from frontline staff
options.b: Partnering with tech hubs and universities, investing in skills and encouraging experimentation
options.c: Copying competitors' products exactly in order to avoid the risk of experimentation
options.d: Banning adoption of new tools until the national infrastructure becomes fully reliable

questions.answer_text: Partnering with tech hubs and universities, investing in skills and encouraging experimentation
questions.explanation: Collaborations, skills and a culture of experimentation help overcome innovation constraints.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which statement about digital transformation is MOST accurate?

options.a: It is limited to marketing campaigns carried out on social media platforms
options.b: It refers to profound organisational change using digital technology to rethink models, processes and customer value
options.c: It is a one-time project that ends when the allocated budget has been spent
options.d: It is the installation of new hardware that replaces older hardware across the organisation

questions.answer_text: It refers to profound organisational change using digital technology to rethink models, processes and customer value
questions.explanation: Digital transformation is strategic, organisation-wide and continuous, not simply a technology installation.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which statement BEST describes IT's role in enabling digital business models?

options.a: IT is relevant only for back-office accounting and payroll processing tasks
options.b: IT replaces the need for a business strategy by selecting the best digital models
options.c: IT provides the infrastructure and tools, such as cloud, data and platforms, that let firms create, deliver and capture value differently
options.d: IT only reduces cost through hardware standardisation and centralised purchasing

questions.answer_text: IT provides the infrastructure and tools, such as cloud, data and platforms, that let firms create, deliver and capture value differently
questions.explanation: IT enables digital business models through cloud, analytics, platforms and connectivity.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which risk is MOST associated with treating IT as a cost centre rather than a strategic asset?

options.a: Too much emphasis on user adoption that slows deployment of new features
options.b: Excess alignment between IT and business goals that restricts technical creativity
options.c: Over-investment that exhausts the innovation budget before projects are completed
options.d: Fragmented efforts that create technical debt, duplication and failed initiatives

questions.answer_text: Fragmented efforts that create technical debt, duplication and failed initiatives
questions.explanation: Without strategic treatment, IT efforts become fragmented and fail to deliver sustained value.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A manufacturer deploys sensors and smart factory systems so machines monitor themselves and predict maintenance. Which industry impact is described?

options.a: Blockchain-based land registries that verify property title records
options.b: IoT and smart factories changing how products are made
options.c: AI chatbots replacing customer service agents in call centres
options.d: Telemedicine consultations that connect remote patients with doctors

questions.answer_text: IoT and smart factories changing how products are made
questions.explanation: IoT and smart factories transform manufacturing through monitoring and predictive maintenance.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: A traditional Nigerian retailer introduces PoS machines and inventory systems. Which statement is MOST accurate?

options.a: Inventory systems only reduce staff numbers and cannot support better decisions
options.b: Basic digital tools streamline workflows and inform decisions, illustrating early-stage digitalisation of an industry
options.c: PoS systems are advanced AI applications rather than basic digital tools
options.d: These tools have no effect on competitiveness because customers rarely notice them

questions.answer_text: Basic digital tools streamline workflows and inform decisions, illustrating early-stage digitalisation of an industry
questions.explanation: Even simple tools like PoS and inventory systems automate tasks and support better decisions.

questions.module_title: Strategic Role of IT in Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which pairing reflects a benefit AND a challenge of digitalisation?

options.a: Slower decision-making and less innovation, alongside improved employee morale
options.b: Reduced data volumes and fewer integration needs, alongside higher operating costs
options.c: Improved efficiency and customer experience; resistance to change and lack of skilled digital talent
options.d: Lower regulation and elimination of cybersecurity risk, alongside slower decision-making

questions.answer_text: Improved efficiency and customer experience; resistance to change and lack of skilled digital talent
questions.explanation: Digitalisation brings efficiency and experience benefits alongside resistance, skills and security challenges.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which description BEST defines a digital strategy?

options.a: A plan aligning digital technologies with business objectives, defining how the organisation competes and creates value in a digital environment
options.b: An annual budget for the replacement of ageing hardware across the organisation
options.c: A list of the software applications that an organisation has purchased and installed
options.d: A technical architecture diagram of the data centre and its network connections

questions.answer_text: A plan aligning digital technologies with business objectives, defining how the organisation competes and creates value in a digital environment
questions.explanation: A digital strategy is a comprehensive plan for using digital technology to achieve business goals and sustain success.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Traditional taxi services in Nigeria were forced to digitise after ride-hailing apps changed customer expectations. Which strategic driver is MOST evident?

options.a: Compliance with a new accounting standard affecting how revenue is reported
options.b: A fall in the cost of paper that made printed documentation more attractive
options.c: A shortage of office space that required firms to consider remote working
options.d: Changing customer expectations and competitive pressure from digital entrants

questions.answer_text: Changing customer expectations and competitive pressure from digital entrants
questions.explanation: Digital entrants and rising customer expectations are strategic drivers pushing firms to transform.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A manufacturer adopts IoT and analytics to forecast demand and cut waste. Which strategic driver does this MOST directly reflect?

options.a: Data-driven decision-making and operational efficiency
options.b: Reduction of customer choice as production becomes more standardised
options.c: Replacement of governance with automated systems that make decisions unaided
options.d: Regulatory exemption for industrial firms that adopt connected technologies

questions.answer_text: Data-driven decision-making and operational efficiency
questions.explanation: Transformation enables data collection, analytics and predictive modelling for better decisions and efficiency.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which contrast between digital strategy and traditional business strategy is MOST accurate?

options.a: Digital strategy treats technology as a core driver of value and disruption, whereas traditional strategy treats it as a support tool
options.b: Digital strategy relies on linear, pipeline-based models, whereas traditional strategy relies on platforms
options.c: Both treat technology identically as a back-office function that supports other activities
options.d: Traditional strategy prioritises digital experience, whereas digital strategy prioritises cost leadership

questions.answer_text: Digital strategy treats technology as a core driver of value and disruption, whereas traditional strategy treats it as a support tool
questions.explanation: The course contrasts technology as support (traditional) with technology as core driver (digital).

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which statement BEST describes a strategic digital roadmap?

options.a: A legal contract with technology vendors that fixes prices and delivery dates
options.b: A high-level visual plan with prioritised initiatives, timelines, owners and KPIs showing how long-term digital goals will be achieved
options.c: A forecast of annual hardware prices used to plan equipment replacement purchases
options.d: A detailed task list for one software deployment, with daily assignments for the project team

questions.answer_text: A high-level visual plan with prioritised initiatives, timelines, owners and KPIs showing how long-term digital goals will be achieved
questions.explanation: A roadmap outlines how an organisation will achieve its digital vision through phased, prioritised initiatives.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which is a key benefit of a well-designed digital roadmap?

options.a: It fixes the plan so that it cannot be changed even when market conditions shift
options.b: It ensures limited time, money and talent are allocated to the most impactful initiatives and enables progress tracking
options.c: It removes the need for governance and KPIs because the plan itself guarantees delivery
options.d: It guarantees that no individual project will fail during the transformation programme

questions.answer_text: It ensures limited time, money and talent are allocated to the most impactful initiatives and enables progress tracking
questions.explanation: Roadmaps focus resources and support continuous tracking through milestones and KPIs.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Toyota's Just-in-Time system reduced inventory and optimised production schedules to cut costs. Which type of innovation is this?

options.a: Process innovation, improving how products are created or delivered
options.b: Business model innovation, changing how value is captured
options.c: Product innovation, launching new features in an existing offering
options.d: Radical innovation, creating an entirely new market segment

questions.answer_text: Process innovation, improving how products are created or delivered
questions.explanation: Process innovation changes production or delivery methods to raise efficiency and quality.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Apple's first iPhone introduced touchscreens and an app ecosystem. Which type of innovation is MOST evident?

options.a: Incremental innovation, making small and continuous design tweaks to an existing phone
options.b: Process innovation, streamlining internal production methods to lower unit costs
options.c: Organisational innovation, restructuring management practices for flatter decision-making
options.d: Product innovation, creating new or significantly improved products and services

questions.answer_text: Product innovation, creating new or significantly improved products and services
questions.explanation: The iPhone is a product innovation with revolutionary features.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Google's practice of allowing employees to spend a day a week on side projects, which led to Gmail, is an example of:

options.a: Process innovation, redesigning manufacturing workflows to reduce unit cost and waste
options.b: Organisational innovation, changing structure or management practices to foster innovation
options.c: Product innovation, improving the interface of an existing messaging application
options.d: Disruptive innovation, entering an underserved low-end market with a cheaper alternative

questions.answer_text: Organisational innovation, changing structure or management practices to foster innovation
questions.explanation: Google's 20% time changed how work is organised to stimulate innovation.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Coca-Cola regularly adjusts its recipe or packaging to meet changing consumer preferences. Which type of innovation is this?

options.a: Disruptive innovation, challenging incumbents with cheaper alternatives
options.b: Business model innovation, changing the revenue model
options.c: Radical innovation, breakthrough that disrupts entire industries
options.d: Incremental innovation, minor continuous improvements to existing products

questions.answer_text: Incremental innovation, minor continuous improvements to existing products
questions.explanation: Small, continuous improvements to existing products are incremental innovation.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Electric vehicle makers introduced sustainable alternatives that created new market segments in the automobile industry. Which type of innovation does this represent?

options.a: Incremental innovation, making small design tweaks to existing vehicle models each year
options.b: Organisational innovation, flattening reporting lines to speed up decision-making
options.c: Process innovation, automating factory production lines to cut manufacturing costs
options.d: Radical innovation, significant breakthroughs introducing new concepts or technologies

questions.answer_text: Radical innovation, significant breakthroughs introducing new concepts or technologies
questions.explanation: Breakthroughs that create entirely new segments are radical innovation.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Uber and Lyft challenged established taxi firms by offering more convenient, lower-cost alternatives through mobile apps. Which concept does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: Organisational innovation, where firms restructure management to cut overheads
options.b: Incremental innovation, where market leaders keep improving existing taxi services
options.c: Open innovation, where firms share research with partners to speed development
options.d: Disruptive innovation, where smaller entrants win by serving underserved needs more affordably

questions.answer_text: Disruptive innovation, where smaller entrants win by serving underserved needs more affordably
questions.explanation: Disruptors gain traction by addressing unmet needs with affordable, accessible solutions.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which situation, viewed through Porter's Five Forces, offers disruptors the BEST opening?

options.a: A market dominated by one firm with exclusive access to all of the customers
options.b: A saturated, complacent market where incumbents are locked into legacy systems and cost structures
options.c: A market protected by high regulatory barriers and heavy capital requirements for entry
options.d: A market with strong supplier power where buyers have no practical alternatives

questions.answer_text: A saturated, complacent market where incumbents are locked into legacy systems and cost structures
questions.explanation: Disruptors exploit complacent rivalry and legacy-bound incumbents with better value propositions.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Airbnb did not replace hotels directly but redefined short-term accommodation. Which force does this MOST clearly illustrate?

options.a: Industry rivalry, by matching the prices charged by established hotel chains
options.b: Bargaining power of suppliers, by controlling the supply of hotel rooms to travellers
options.c: Threat of new entrants, by building physical barriers that block hotel competitors
options.d: Threat of substitutes, by redefining how value is delivered rather than copying the incumbent

questions.answer_text: Threat of substitutes, by redefining how value is delivered rather than copying the incumbent
questions.explanation: Airbnb redefined the way accommodation is offered, a substitute rather than a like-for-like competitor.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A digital platform enters a market with minimal investment, using cloud services to scale rapidly against brick-and-mortar firms. Which force is MOST relevant?

options.a: Bargaining power of suppliers, since essential inputs are scarce and controlled
options.b: Threat of new entrants, since low barriers such as minimal regulation or capital let disruptors enter
options.c: Bargaining power of customers, since buyers in the market are few and concentrated
options.d: Industry rivalry, since established firms avoid price competition in mature markets

questions.answer_text: Threat of new entrants, since low barriers such as minimal regulation or capital let disruptors enter
questions.explanation: Low barriers to entry allow disruptors to launch with minimal investment and scale using cloud.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A large R&D organisation wants a structured process with sequential stages and go or kill decision points to manage risk and resources. Which framework fits BEST?

options.a: Agile innovation
options.b: Open innovation
options.c: Stage-gate model
options.d: Lean startup

questions.answer_text: Stage-gate model
questions.explanation: The stage-gate model controls progress through stages and decision gates.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A team builds a minimum viable product, measures customer response and pivots based on feedback. Which framework is this?

options.a: Design thinking, using empathy interviews only
options.b: Lean startup, using Build-Measure-Learn loops
options.c: Open innovation, using external patents
options.d: Stage-gate model, using go or kill gates

questions.answer_text: Lean startup, using Build-Measure-Learn loops
questions.explanation: Lean startup uses MVPs and the Build-Measure-Learn loop to learn fast with minimal waste.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A bank redesigns its mobile app by interviewing users, prototyping repeatedly and testing solutions with customers. Which framework is MOST evident?

options.a: Open innovation, with external partners co-developing the new solution
options.b: Stage-gate model, with sequential stages and go or kill decisions at defined gates
options.c: Business process reengineering, with a radical redesign of end-to-end workflows
options.d: Design thinking, empathy-driven, iterative and human-centred problem solving

questions.answer_text: Design thinking, empathy-driven, iterative and human-centred problem solving
questions.explanation: Design thinking centres on understanding user needs through empathy, prototyping and iteration.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A telecom with limited internal R&D partners with start-ups and universities to co-develop new services. Which framework applies?

options.a: Stage-gate model, which gates internal projects through formal decision points
options.b: Lean startup, which builds a minimum viable product internally and then pivots
options.c: Agile innovation, which runs iterative internal sprints with cross-functional teams
options.d: Open innovation, leveraging external partners and ecosystems to speed development

questions.answer_text: Open innovation, leveraging external partners and ecosystems to speed development
questions.explanation: Open innovation draws on external knowledge and resources beyond internal limits.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: A software company releases features in short sprints with cross-functional teams and adapts to feedback quickly. Which framework is this?

options.a: Open innovation, which depends on external partners for knowledge and resources
options.b: Design thinking, which maps user empathy before prototyping new solutions
options.c: Stage-gate model, which moves projects through sequential stages with formal gates
options.d: Agile innovation, iterative sprints and continuous delivery

questions.answer_text: Agile innovation, iterative sprints and continuous delivery
questions.explanation: Agile innovation emphasises speed, adaptability and flexibility in dynamic markets.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which action is a recommended way to IDENTIFY technological disruption early?

options.a: Wait for competitors to react first and then follow their chosen strategy closely
options.b: Assume that current customers will never change their preferences or expectations
options.c: Reduce spending on market research in order to cut costs during uncertain periods
options.d: Monitor emerging technologies, listen to changing customer preferences and follow thought leaders

questions.answer_text: Monitor emerging technologies, listen to changing customer preferences and follow thought leaders
questions.explanation: Early signals appear in emerging technology and changes in customer behaviour.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Google's acquisition of YouTube is an example of which response to disruption?

options.a: Lobbying regulators to introduce rules that block the new entrant from the market
options.b: Ignoring the new technology until it has matured and competitors have adopted it
options.c: Partnering with or acquiring companies that specialise in disruptive technologies
options.d: Cutting prices on existing services to discourage customers from switching

questions.answer_text: Partnering with or acquiring companies that specialise in disruptive technologies
questions.explanation: Partnerships and acquisitions let firms access disruptive capabilities.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which capability allows a company to experiment, iterate and pivot quickly when technology shifts?

options.a: Organisational agility
options.b: Rigid hierarchical control
options.c: Standardised annual planning
options.d: Long-term fixed contracts

questions.answer_text: Organisational agility
questions.explanation: Being agile helps a company respond to market change by experimenting and pivoting.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Cloud computing disrupted traditional data centres. What should an incumbent hardware provider do FIRST according to the course's guidance?

options.a: Lay off staff in order to protect short-term profits and delay investment
options.b: Scan emerging technologies and customer shifts to recognise the disruption early, then invest in skills and partnerships
options.c: Increase hardware prices to protect margins while customers gradually move away
options.d: Deny the disruption until market share has dropped sharply, then react with cost cuts

questions.answer_text: Scan emerging technologies and customer shifts to recognise the disruption early, then invest in skills and partnerships
questions.explanation: Early recognition followed by capability building and partnering is the recommended response.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which statement BEST defines business model innovation?

options.a: Adding new hardware to the existing infrastructure to increase capacity
options.b: Making incremental improvements to an existing product based on customer feedback
options.c: Developing new ways to create, deliver and capture value, such as new revenue streams, pricing models or channels
options.d: Reducing prices on existing services in order to protect market share

questions.answer_text: Developing new ways to create, deliver and capture value, such as new revenue streams, pricing models or channels
questions.explanation: It rethinks how a company makes money and delivers value in response to change.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Spotify offers a free tier with ads and a paid premium tier. Which business model feature is this?

options.a: A pure subscription model with no free access to any part of the service
options.b: A franchise model in which partners sell the service under the brand
options.c: Freemium model, offering basic service free and charging for premium features
options.d: A one-time licence model in which users pay once for permanent access

questions.answer_text: Freemium model, offering basic service free and charging for premium features
questions.explanation: Spotify's freemium service attracts users and converts some to paid plans.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Why do digital platforms such as Uber and Airbnb benefit from network effects?

options.a: Each additional participant increases value for others, which helps sustain growth and competitive advantage
options.b: They avoid collecting data in order to protect the privacy of every participant
options.c: They reduce the number of participants in order to improve the quality of each interaction
options.d: They rely on owning physical infrastructure that competitors cannot easily replicate

questions.answer_text: Each additional participant increases value for others, which helps sustain growth and competitive advantage
questions.explanation: Platforms connect both sides of a market; more users make the platform more valuable.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Netflix used a digital platform to move from DVD rental to on-demand streaming. Which concept does this BEST illustrate?

options.a: Process innovation limited to warehouse and logistics operations
options.b: Incremental updates to packaging and disc design for rental products
options.c: Business model innovation through digital platforms that enable new value delivery
options.d: Cost leadership achieved through lower rent for retail locations

questions.answer_text: Business model innovation through digital platforms that enable new value delivery
questions.explanation: Netflix changed how it delivers and monetises content using a platform.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which is a challenge of business model innovation using digital platforms?

options.a: Absence of competition from other platforms once the first mover has launched
options.b: Regulatory and trust issues, competition and the need for scalable technology and data governance
options.c: Freedom from dependence on network effects, since the platform needs few users
options.d: Guaranteed customer loyalty without further investment, because platforms are naturally sticky

questions.answer_text: Regulatory and trust issues, competition and the need for scalable technology and data governance
questions.explanation: Platform models face regulatory, competition, trust and technology challenges.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Amazon's roadmap extended from retail into AWS, Prime Video and AI-powered delivery to enhance customer experience. What does this case BEST illustrate?

options.a: A strategic digital roadmap that diversifies capabilities and builds an ecosystem around customer experience
options.b: A purely cost-cutting approach focused on reducing delivery and staffing costs
options.c: A single-product retail model with no expansion into new capability areas
options.d: A strategy based on avoiding technology investment so that costs remain low

questions.answer_text: A strategic digital roadmap that diversifies capabilities and builds an ecosystem around customer experience
questions.explanation: Amazon's roadmap shows long-term, ecosystem-based expansion driven by customer experience.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which element belongs in the formulation of a digital strategy?

options.a: Only a list of hardware purchases and the schedule for their installation
options.b: Only vendor contracts and the pricing terms agreed with each technology supplier
options.c: Only the marketing calendar for the digital channels the firm plans to use
options.d: A clear vision, defined digital capabilities, and governance and policies that guide execution

questions.answer_text: A clear vision, defined digital capabilities, and governance and policies that guide execution
questions.explanation: A digital strategy articulates vision, capabilities, governance and an implementation plan.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which is a core strategic driver that pushes businesses to digitise?

options.a: Evolving customer expectations, competitive pressure and the need for data-driven decisions
options.b: Reduction of employee numbers as the only objective of the transformation
options.c: Elimination of customer data collection to avoid regulatory interaction
options.d: A desire to increase paper usage and physical record keeping across departments

questions.answer_text: Evolving customer expectations, competitive pressure and the need for data-driven decisions
questions.explanation: Customer expectations, competition and data-driven insight drive digital strategy.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which effect is a typical consequence of industry disruption for incumbents?

options.a: Reduced customer expectations as the industry matures and prices stabilise
options.b: Market realignment, pressure on pricing models and a need for agility
options.c: Fewer competitors and slower change as the market consolidates around leaders
options.d: Guaranteed stability of revenue because customers rarely change established suppliers

questions.answer_text: Market realignment, pressure on pricing models and a need for agility
questions.explanation: Disruption realigns markets, pressures pricing and demands agility.

questions.module_title: Digital Strategy and Innovation Management
questions.question: Which statement about a roadmap's content is MOST accurate?

options.a: It contains only technical specifications for the systems that will be deployed
options.b: It is a fixed contract that cannot be revised once approved by the executive board
options.c: It replaces the need for KPIs because the timeline already shows progress
options.d: It lists prioritised initiatives with timelines, responsible teams and mechanisms to monitor progress

questions.answer_text: It lists prioritised initiatives with timelines, responsible teams and mechanisms to monitor progress
questions.explanation: A roadmap guides execution through prioritised, owned, tracked initiatives.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which statement BEST defines change management in digital transformation?

options.a: A technical process of installing software updates across devices and servers
options.b: A financial tool for budgeting and approving new technology projects
options.c: A structured approach to transitioning individuals, teams and organisations from a current to a desired state with minimal disruption
options.d: A legal procedure for the early termination of vendor contracts

questions.answer_text: A structured approach to transitioning individuals, teams and organisations from a current to a desired state with minimal disruption
questions.explanation: Change management guides people through change to maximise adoption of new technologies and processes.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which factor MOST directly reduces uncertainty and resistance during a digital change programme?

options.a: Relying on a single announcement on go-live day to explain all of the changes
options.b: Reducing training in order to speed delivery of the new platform to users
options.c: Strong leadership support with clear communication of the reasons for change
options.d: Limiting information to staff until implementation is complete to avoid early concerns

questions.answer_text: Strong leadership support with clear communication of the reasons for change
questions.explanation: Leadership support and clear communication reduce uncertainty and build ownership.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which model describes change through Unfreeze, Change and Refreeze?

options.a: ADKAR model
options.b: McKinsey 7-S framework
options.c: Kotter's eight-step model
options.d: Lewin's three-stage model

questions.answer_text: Lewin's three-stage model
questions.explanation: Lewin's model prepares for change, implements it and stabilises new practices.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A programme leader creates urgency, builds a guiding coalition, develops a vision, enables action, generates short-term wins and anchors the change. Which model is this?

options.a: Lewin's three-stage model
options.b: Agile change management
options.c: ADKAR model
options.d: Kotter's 8-step change model

questions.answer_text: Kotter's 8-step change model
questions.explanation: Those steps summarise Kotter's change model.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which model focuses on individual change through Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement?

options.a: Kotter's model
options.b: ADKAR model
options.c: Lewin's model
options.d: McKinsey 7-S framework

questions.answer_text: ADKAR model
questions.explanation: ADKAR addresses how individuals move through change.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which set lists the seven elements aligned in the McKinsey 7-S framework?

options.a: Strategy, Speed, Scale, Security, Support, Systems and Skills
options.b: Structure, Stability, Staff, Status, Style, Systems and Standards
options.c: Strategy, Structure, Systems, Shared Values, Style, Staff and Skills
options.d: Strategy, Sales, Service, Skills, Staff, Style and Success

questions.answer_text: Strategy, Structure, Systems, Shared Values, Style, Staff and Skills
questions.explanation: The 7-S framework aligns Strategy, Structure, Systems, Shared Values, Style, Staff and Skills.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Lewin's model is MOST suitable when:

options.a: The change focuses on individual emotions rather than on organisational preparation
options.b: The change is continuous and ongoing, with no defined end state or completion date
options.c: The change is clearly defined and has a definite start and end, such as a system upgrade
options.d: The change is a cultural shift of unknown duration across the whole organisation

questions.answer_text: The change is clearly defined and has a definite start and end, such as a system upgrade
questions.explanation: Lewin's simple linear model suits well-defined changes but is too simplistic for complex ongoing transformation.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A criticism of Kotter's model is that it:

options.a: Ignores the need for a clear vision and communication of the change to staff
options.b: Has no role for short-term wins or for anchoring change in organisational culture
options.c: Focuses only on individual adoption and neglects leadership and organisational aspects
options.d: Assumes change is linear and top-down, requiring strong leadership and a cultural shift

questions.answer_text: Assumes change is linear and top-down, requiring strong leadership and a cultural shift
questions.explanation: The course notes Kotter assumes change is linear and top-down and can be time-consuming.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A criticism of ADKAR is that it:

options.a: Requires no individual engagement because change is driven by top management
options.b: Applies only to technology firms because it assumes a software-based change
options.c: Ignores the awareness stage so employees never learn why a change is necessary
options.d: Does not focus on organisational or strategic aspects, concentrating on individual adoption

questions.answer_text: Does not focus on organisational or strategic aspects, concentrating on individual adoption
questions.explanation: ADKAR is individual-focused and less useful for strategic, organisation-wide aspects.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Employees fear job losses and distrust management's motives for a new platform. Which approach BEST reduces such resistance?

options.a: Delay training until errors occur so that staff see the need for it
options.b: Announce the system on go-live day with no discussion, to avoid early objections
options.c: Replace employees who voice concerns so that resistance does not spread
options.d: Involve staff early, communicate the 'why', provide training and create feedback channels

questions.answer_text: Involve staff early, communicate the 'why', provide training and create feedback channels
questions.explanation: Participation, communication, training and feedback reduce resistance.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which is a KEY cause of resistance to digital transformation?

options.a: Too much involvement of staff in decisions about how the change will work
options.b: Fear of job loss, lack of skills, comfort with existing processes and poor communication
options.c: Overly transparent leadership that exposes uncertainty about the programme
options.d: Excessive training that exhausts staff before the new system is introduced

questions.answer_text: Fear of job loss, lack of skills, comfort with existing processes and poor communication
questions.explanation: Resistance arises from fear, skill gaps, habit and unclear communication.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which statement BEST defines customer experience (CX)?

options.a: The number of products a company sells across its digital and physical channels
options.b: The speed of a company's website measured during peak shopping periods
options.c: The price of a product compared with the prices charged by competitors
options.d: The overall perception a customer forms of a brand based on all interactions across channels and over time

questions.answer_text: The overall perception a customer forms of a brand based on all interactions across channels and over time
questions.explanation: CX is the cumulative impact of all customer interactions with a brand.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which principle supports seamless CX design in a digital environment?

options.a: Complex multi-step forms intended to gather as much customer data as possible
options.b: Separate processes for each channel, each following its own rules and standards
options.c: A simplified user journey with consistent experience across channels and mobile-first accessibility
options.d: Desktop-only design that assumes customers use large screens at all times

questions.answer_text: A simplified user journey with consistent experience across channels and mobile-first accessibility
questions.explanation: Seamless CX relies on simplicity, consistency and mobile accessibility.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Why is CX a strategic differentiator in the digital age?

options.a: Customers no longer value convenience because they expect the lowest price
options.b: Technology removes the need for service because customers are self-sufficient
options.c: Customer expectations are high and switching costs are low, so seamless experiences build loyalty and retention
options.d: Competition has fallen as technology has made markets more concentrated

questions.answer_text: Customer expectations are high and switching costs are low, so seamless experiences build loyalty and retention
questions.explanation: With low switching costs, experience drives retention and profitability.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A retailer wants to track every customer interaction, segment customers and personalise follow-ups across channels. Which tool category is MOST appropriate?

options.a: A hardware inventory register that records the store devices and their locations
options.b: An accounting ledger that records supplier invoices and tracks payment schedules
options.c: A project scheduling tool that sequences delivery tasks and tracks resource allocation
options.d: A CRM platform that centralises customer data and interaction history

questions.answer_text: A CRM platform that centralises customer data and interaction history
questions.explanation: CRM systems store customer data and support personalised engagement and analysis.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A bank wants to answer routine customer queries at any hour and guide users through simple tasks without adding agents. Which tool BEST fits?

options.a: Internal payroll software that automates salary payments and tax deductions for staff
options.b: Branch queue-management displays that direct customers to the next available teller
options.c: Chatbots and live chat tools that respond in real time and escalate when needed
options.d: Quarterly printed newsletters mailed to customers with updates on products and services

questions.answer_text: Chatbots and live chat tools that respond in real time and escalate when needed
questions.explanation: Chatbots and live chat provide real-time support and guidance at scale.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A firm uses surveys and post-interaction feedback forms to improve products and services. Which CX practice is this?

options.a: Gathering and analysing customer feedback to drive continuous improvement
options.b: Reducing communication with customers to lower the volume of complaints received
options.c: Replacing analytics with intuition so that managers can respond to complaints faster
options.d: Outsourcing all service operations so that feedback is handled entirely by vendors

questions.answer_text: Gathering and analysing customer feedback to drive continuous improvement
questions.explanation: Customer feedback is vital for improving offerings and satisfaction.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A bank introduces a new digital onboarding process but staff keep using the old paper process and customers complain of delays. Which statement BEST explains the link between change management and CX?

options.a: Customers are unaffected by internal process change as long as prices remain stable
options.b: CX is independent of employee behaviour, because customers see only the digital interface
options.c: Change management is relevant only to IT staff who maintain the onboarding system
options.d: Without internal adoption, customers do not receive the intended value, so change management determines CX outcomes

questions.answer_text: Without internal adoption, customers do not receive the intended value, so change management determines CX outcomes
questions.explanation: Employee adoption of new tools and processes decides whether the CX value is delivered.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which description shows cultural alignment between change management and CX?

options.a: A culture focused only on internal efficiency, with customer outcomes handled by sales teams
options.b: A culture that avoids customer feedback so that staff can concentrate on process tasks
options.c: A customer-first culture embedded during transformation so mindsets and values shift toward customer outcomes
options.d: A culture limited to the IT department, with other units following existing practices

questions.answer_text: A customer-first culture embedded during transformation so mindsets and values shift toward customer outcomes
questions.explanation: Embedding customer-first values during change aligns internal transformation with external experience.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which practice BEST integrates change management with CX during a rollout?

options.a: Remove journey maps from the project plan to save time during the rollout phase
options.b: Release all changes at once with no feedback loop so that customers see a finished product
options.c: Limit testing to the vendor so that internal staff are not distracted from daily work
options.d: Use journey maps to identify pain points and release changes iteratively with feedback from customers and staff

questions.answer_text: Use journey maps to identify pain points and release changes iteratively with feedback from customers and staff
questions.explanation: Journey mapping and iterative delivery align transformation with customer and employee feedback.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which leadership behaviour MOST strongly shapes a customer-first culture?

options.a: Avoiding visible involvement in the programme so that teams feel free to experiment
options.b: Focusing exclusively on cost targets so that staff understand what matters to the board
options.c: Modelling adaptability, empathy and customer-first thinking through consistent actions and communication
options.d: Delegating all communication about the change to HR so that leaders stay focused on strategy

questions.answer_text: Modelling adaptability, empathy and customer-first thinking through consistent actions and communication
questions.explanation: Leaders influence culture through behaviour; consistent communication reduces resistance.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A leader links internal goals such as process automation to external outcomes like faster customer service. Which leadership role is shown?

options.a: Auditing legal compliance
options.b: Controlling budgets only
options.c: Managing hardware vendors
options.d: Connecting internal change goals with external customer outcomes

questions.answer_text: Connecting internal change goals with external customer outcomes
questions.explanation: Effective leaders articulate how internal change delivers customer value.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which set lists core components of a strategic digital transformation roadmap?

options.a: Vendor lists, office floor plans, travel schedules and the budget for staff social events
options.b: Vision and objectives, prioritised initiatives, timelines and milestones, governance and KPIs, and change and capability building
options.c: Server specifications, cable layouts, rack designs and the data centre cooling plan
options.d: Daily task lists for the help desk, shift rotas and the escalation call tree

questions.answer_text: Vision and objectives, prioritised initiatives, timelines and milestones, governance and KPIs, and change and capability building
questions.explanation: A roadmap combines vision, initiatives, timing, oversight mechanisms and people-related enablers.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A programme office is told its roadmap is "just a Gantt chart." Which response is MOST accurate?

options.a: It is a living framework aligning digital initiatives with strategy, resources and outcomes, not just a project plan
options.b: Roadmaps must never change once approved, because revisions undermine accountability
options.c: It is correct, because roadmaps contain only schedules of tasks and delivery dates
options.d: Roadmaps should not link to strategic goals, because strategy changes too often

questions.answer_text: It is a living framework aligning digital initiatives with strategy, resources and outcomes, not just a project plan
questions.explanation: The roadmap is a living strategic framework rather than a static schedule.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which is a benefit of a strategic digital transformation roadmap?

options.a: Ensures that every project in the programme will be delivered on time and on budget
options.b: Eliminates change management needs because staff follow the documented timeline
options.c: Removes the need for leadership sponsorship because the plan drives the programme forward
options.d: Prioritises high-impact projects, provides a structured path and reduces resistance and strategic drift

questions.answer_text: Prioritises high-impact projects, provides a structured path and reduces resistance and strategic drift
questions.explanation: Roadmaps focus effort, structure the path and reduce drift and resistance.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A pilot in one branch tests a new mobile workflow before bank-wide rollout. Which change management strategy is this?

options.a: Big-bang deployment with no testing so that all users adopt the new workflow together
options.b: Retroactive training after go-live once users have reported the main difficulties
options.c: Pilot programmes that test changes on a small scale and gather feedback before scaling
options.d: Withholding information about the new workflow until the full rollout is announced

questions.answer_text: Pilot programmes that test changes on a small scale and gather feedback before scaling
questions.explanation: Pilots reduce risk by testing and refining changes before wider adoption.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which statement about change in digital transformation is MOST accurate?

options.a: Change always succeeds if the technology is advanced enough and the budget is adequate
options.b: Change management is needed only for small projects where few people are affected
options.c: Change is unrelated to culture, because culture influences only day-to-day working habits
options.d: Change is inevitable but its success is not, so organisations need agility, learning and structured approaches

questions.answer_text: Change is inevitable but its success is not, so organisations need agility, learning and structured approaches
questions.explanation: The course stresses that adaptation and structured change management determine success.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: Which strategy is MOST effective for addressing resistance rooted in unfamiliarity with new tools?

options.a: Mandating use through disciplinary action so that staff adopt the tools without delay

options.c: Targeted training and upskilling combined with support and champions
options.d: Limiting communication to email announcements so that messages stay consistent

questions.answer_text: Targeted training and upskilling combined with support and champions
questions.explanation: Training and support address skill and confidence gaps that drive resistance.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A company wants to send personalised campaigns automatically based on customer behaviour. Which tool category supports this?

options.a: Backup and replication software that protects data against hardware failure
options.b: Email marketing and automation platforms such as Mailchimp or SendGrid
options.c: Graphic design tools used to produce marketing images and brand materials

questions.answer_text: Email marketing and automation platforms such as Mailchimp or SendGrid
questions.explanation: Email marketing tools allow personalised, automated campaigns and analytics.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
questions.question: A telecom trains agents on a new CRM but never explains how it improves customer journeys, so agents use it only to log calls. Which gap is MOST evident?

options.a: Staff adoption is not linked to customer value, so the intended CX benefit is lost
options.b: The telecom has too many customer journeys for the CRM to map accurately
options.c: Customers are unaware that the telecom operates a CRM system behind the scenes
options.d: The CRM lacks enough storage capacity to hold the records of the customer base

questions.answer_text: Staff adoption is not linked to customer value, so the intended CX benefit is lost
questions.explanation: Change efforts must connect new tools to customer outcomes for CX value to be realised.

questions.module_title: Change Management and Customer Experience Design
