questions.question: After creating urgency and a guiding coalition, a bank cultivates cross-functional teams that keep proposing digital improvements. Which outcome from Kotter's model does this show?

options.a: Sustained innovation and a mindset shift because staff understand the "why"
options.b: A reduction in the need for leadership, because teams now manage the change themselves
options.c: Elimination of all resistance permanently, because staff understand the vision
options.d: Immediate completion of the transformation, because the coalition delivers short-term wins

questions.answer_text: Sustained innovation and a mindset shift because staff understand the "why"
questions.explanation: Applying Kotter's steps shifted mindsets and embedded innovation.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which trait is MOST essential for leaders guiding digital transformation?

options.a: Visionary, adaptable and technologically fluent, able to create a culture that supports innovation
options.b: Avoidance of technology so that decisions rest on traditional experience and judgment
options.c: Strict control of information so that staff receive messages only through management
options.d: A focus on short-term cost cutting so that the programme demonstrates quick savings

questions.answer_text: Visionary, adaptable and technologically fluent, able to create a culture that supports innovation
questions.explanation: Digital leaders combine vision, adaptability and tech fluency to lead change.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which statement BEST explains why KPIs matter in digital transformation?

options.a: They measure only financial results and ignore customer and process outcomes
options.b: They replace the need for strategy, because targets alone determine what to do
options.c: They enable data-driven decisions, uncover gaps, align stakeholders and ensure accountability
options.d: They are required only by regulators, who use them to assess compliance

questions.answer_text: They enable data-driven decisions, uncover gaps, align stakeholders and ensure accountability
questions.explanation: KPIs quantify progress and guide strategic decisions throughout transformation.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: A mobile banking app tracks daily active users, retention rate and conversion rate. Which KPI category is this?

options.a: Technology adoption and user engagement KPIs
options.b: Environmental KPIs such as energy use and carbon emissions per transaction
options.c: Financial KPIs such as revenue growth, operating margin and cost savings
options.d: Governance KPIs such as audit findings and policy exceptions closed on time

questions.answer_text: Technology adoption and user engagement KPIs
questions.explanation: DAU, retention and conversion measure how users engage with a digital product.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: A firm measures employee engagement, digital skills and participation in digital initiatives. Which KPI category is this?

options.a: Customer KPIs
options.b: Technology infrastructure KPIs
options.c: People KPIs
options.d: Process KPIs

questions.answer_text: People KPIs
questions.explanation: People KPIs evaluate workforce engagement, skills and adaptability.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: A firm tracks process cycle time, error rates and cost per transaction after automation. Which KPI category is this?

options.a: Customer KPIs
options.b: Cultural KPIs
options.c: Process KPIs
options.d: People KPIs

questions.answer_text: Process KPIs
questions.explanation: Process KPIs assess how efficiently processes run during and after transformation.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: A bank tracks mobile app adoption rate, digital transaction volume and customer satisfaction (CSAT). What do these KPIs MOST directly measure?

options.a: The quantity of IT hardware deployed at each of the bank's branch locations
options.b: The effectiveness of digital initiatives from a customer and usage perspective
options.c: The legal compliance of vendor contracts signed during the digital programme
options.d: The strength of employee culture only, based on survey results about workplace values

questions.answer_text: The effectiveness of digital initiatives from a customer and usage perspective
questions.explanation: These KPIs show adoption and customer outcomes of digital transformation.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which metric shows how long a task takes from start to finish and helps forecasting?

options.a: Headcount
options.b: Burn-down
options.c: Velocity
options.d: Cycle time

questions.answer_text: Cycle time
questions.explanation: Cycle time measures how long a work item takes to complete.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which visual tracks remaining work in a sprint over time?

options.a: Org chart
options.b: Gantt chart
options.c: Heat map
options.d: Burn-down chart

questions.answer_text: Burn-down chart
questions.explanation: A burn-down chart shows remaining work and helps gauge whether the team will finish on time.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Spotify's Squad Health Check uses which approach?

options.a: Complex financial formulas that calculate the cost of each team's contribution
options.b: Simple red, yellow and green indicators to assess team health areas
options.c: Hardware performance benchmarks that compare team laptops and network speeds
options.d: Annual employee surveys that rank teams on satisfaction and compensation

questions.answer_text: Simple red, yellow and green indicators to assess team health areas
questions.explanation: It is a lightweight tool using colour codes to assess areas such as teamwork and delivery.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which innovation measure compares financial returns with the amount invested in innovation?

options.a: Return on Innovation Investment (ROII)
options.b: Cycle time
options.c: Number of ideas submitted
options.d: Employee satisfaction

questions.answer_text: Return on Innovation Investment (ROII)
questions.explanation: ROII shows the financial return relative to innovation spending.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which metric is an INPUT measure of innovation?

options.a: Market share gained in segments where the new offering was introduced
options.b: Customer satisfaction scores measured after the launch of a new service
options.c: Revenue from new products launched in the last financial year
options.d: Time and budget allocated to innovation

questions.answer_text: Time and budget allocated to innovation
questions.explanation: Input metrics track resources invested; outputs and impact track results.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which metric tracks how long it takes to go from idea to launch?

options.a: Number of patents
options.b: Employee retention rate
options.c: Cycle time for innovation
options.d: Return on innovation investment

questions.answer_text: Cycle time for innovation
questions.explanation: Cycle time for innovation measures speed from idea to market.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Which strategy helps ensure transformation becomes a lasting capability rather than a one-time event?

options.a: Stopping KPI reviews once the original targets have been reached by the teams
options.b: Embedding continuous training, feedback collection and performance monitoring into operations and culture
options.c: Reducing support after go-live to cut costs once the system is in operation
options.d: Declaring success after the initial rollout so that attention moves to other priorities

questions.answer_text: Embedding continuous training, feedback collection and performance monitoring into operations and culture
questions.explanation: Sustained effort through training, feedback and monitoring keeps momentum.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Why must transformation address Schein's assumptions and values and not only artifacts such as new tools?

options.a: Assumptions change automatically when new tools are introduced to the workplace
options.b: Values are fixed and cannot be changed by any programme or leadership action
options.c: Tools alone do not change deep beliefs, so sustainable change requires shifting values and assumptions
options.d: Artifacts are irrelevant to culture, because culture exists only in unspoken beliefs

questions.answer_text: Tools alone do not change deep beliefs, so sustainable change requires shifting values and assumptions
questions.explanation: Sustainable change must reach deeper levels of culture.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Tony Elumelu's leadership is used in the course as an example of what?

options.a: Digital leadership that is visionary, connected and responsive to rapid change
options.b: A traditional command-and-control approach that relies on instructions from the top
options.c: A short-term cost manager who prioritises quarterly savings above long-term change
options.d: A leader who avoids technology and delegates all digital choices to specialists

questions.answer_text: Digital leadership that is visionary, connected and responsive to rapid change
questions.explanation: The course uses him as an example of visionary leadership in a digital context.

questions.module_title: Organisational Culture and KPIs for Digital Transformation
questions.question: Why should organisations define KPIs at the start of a transformation rather than at the end?

options.a: Because KPIs are needed only for audits at the end of the programme
options.b: So progress can be tracked from the beginning, gaps uncovered early and accountability assigned
options.c: Because metrics change nothing and are separate from decision-making and delivery
options.d: To avoid measuring failures that could embarrass the transformation sponsors

questions.answer_text: So progress can be tracked from the beginning, gaps uncovered early and accountability assigned
questions.explanation: Early KPI definition enables ongoing data-driven decisions.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which technology combination is MOST associated with Industry 4.0?

options.a: Cyber-physical systems, IoT, big data analytics, AI and cloud computing
options.b: Mainframes, punch cards and batch processing used by large organisations
options.c: Telegraph, fax machines and printed catalogues for communicating with customers
options.d: Steam engines, mechanical looms and water-powered production equipment

questions.answer_text: Cyber-physical systems, IoT, big data analytics, AI and cloud computing
questions.explanation: Industry 4.0 fuses physical systems with IoT, analytics, AI and cloud.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which characteristic of Industry 4.0 allows machines, devices, sensors and people to communicate through standard protocols?

options.a: Interoperability
options.b: Decentralised decision-making
options.c: Information transparency
options.d: Technical assistance

questions.answer_text: Interoperability
questions.explanation: Interoperability is seamless communication among machines and humans.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Systems collect comprehensive data to create virtual models of the physical world. Which characteristic is this?

options.a: Interoperability
options.b: Technical assistance
options.c: Decentralised decision-making
options.d: Information transparency

questions.answer_text: Information transparency
questions.explanation: Sensor data creates virtual models enabling informed decisions.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Machines autonomously make routine decisions without human intervention. Which characteristic is this?

options.a: Information transparency
options.b: Decentralised decision-making
options.c: Technical assistance
options.d: Interoperability

questions.answer_text: Decentralised decision-making
questions.explanation: Cyber-physical systems can decide and execute tasks autonomously.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Systems aggregate and visualise data to help humans make decisions and perform hazardous or exhausting tasks. Which characteristic is this?

options.a: Technical assistance
options.b: Information transparency
options.c: Interoperability
options.d: Decentralised decision-making

questions.answer_text: Technical assistance
questions.explanation: Technical assistance supports humans with data and by performing difficult tasks.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which technology builds three-dimensional products layer by layer from digital models, enabling customisation and less waste?

options.a: Blockchain
options.b: Cloud computing
options.c: Additive manufacturing (3D printing)
options.d: Augmented reality

questions.answer_text: Additive manufacturing (3D printing)
questions.explanation: 3D printing fabricates objects directly from digital models.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which technology overlays digital information on real-world settings to support assembly and maintenance?

options.a: Virtual reality
options.b: Big data
options.c: Edge routing
options.d: Augmented reality

questions.answer_text: Augmented reality
questions.explanation: AR overlays digital information; VR creates simulated environments.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: A factory uses predictive maintenance to avoid unplanned downtime. Which benefit of Industry 4.0 is MOST direct?

options.a: Cost reduction through lower repair costs and less downtime
options.b: Higher paper usage as maintenance logs are printed and filed by technicians
options.c: Slower innovation cycles because testing now requires more manual checks
options.d: Reduced product customisation as machines are limited to fixed product designs

questions.answer_text: Cost reduction through lower repair costs and less downtime
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance reduces unplanned downtime and repair costs.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Smart manufacturing systems adapt quickly to changes in product design and batch size. Which benefit is this?

options.a: Reduced automation because machines are controlled manually for each product change
options.b: Increased flexibility and mass customisation
options.c: Higher inventory needs because products are made in large fixed quantities
options.d: Longer lead times because production lines must be reset between batches

questions.answer_text: Increased flexibility and mass customisation
questions.explanation: Smart systems adapt to demand, enabling customised production.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which application of cyber-physical systems involves a virtual replica of an asset used to simulate and optimise performance?

options.a: Digital twin
options.b: Intranet portal
options.c: Data warehouse
options.d: Email gateway

questions.answer_text: Digital twin
questions.explanation: Digital twins are virtual replicas that support simulation and predictive maintenance.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which sequence best describes how an IoT system operates?

options.a: Devices ignore the data they collect and wait for instructions from a central operator
options.b: Analysts collect data by hand, store it on paper and later enter it into reports
options.c: Sensors collect data, networks transmit it, cloud or local systems process it, and insights trigger actions
options.d: Cloud systems collect data, sensors process it, and humans transmit the results manually

questions.answer_text: Sensors collect data, networks transmit it, cloud or local systems process it, and insights trigger actions
questions.explanation: IoT involves sensing, transmission, processing and action.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: A logistics firm tracks shipments in real time with connected devices to improve its supply chain. Which IoT business application is this?

options.a: Digital identity
options.b: Smart home automation
options.c: Telemedicine
options.d: Supply chain tracking

questions.answer_text: Supply chain tracking
questions.explanation: IoT enables real-time tracking in logistics and supply chains.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which challenge of Industry 4.0 and IoT implementation does the course highlight?

options.a: Excess skilled labour, free infrastructure and a clear return on every investment
options.b: Absence of data, abundant standards and automatic compatibility with legacy systems
options.c: Universal expertise, no security concerns and complete certainty about returns
options.d: Data security and privacy, legacy systems, skills shortages and uncertain return on investment

questions.answer_text: Data security and privacy, legacy systems, skills shortages and uncertain return on investment
questions.explanation: Implementation challenges include security, legacy integration, skills and ROI.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which approach BEST addresses IoT implementation challenges?

options.a: Align IoT with business goals, set governance, encourage IT and operations collaboration, use agile project management and define data policies
options.b: Avoid governance to speed delivery, relying on vendors to set data policies
options.c: Deploy devices first and plan later, so that data can show where value arises
options.d: Keep IT and operations separate to preserve clear and distinct responsibilities

questions.answer_text: Align IoT with business goals, set governance, encourage IT and operations collaboration, use agile project management and define data policies
questions.explanation: Structured alignment and governance help overcome IoT challenges.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which cultural shift is MOST important for Industry 4.0 success?

options.a: Agility, lifelong learning, collaboration across silos and willingness to reskill
options.b: Resistance to technology so that existing operating procedures remain stable
options.c: Reliance on legacy processes so that staff are not disrupted by retraining
options.d: Strict departmental separation so that each unit controls its own tools and data

questions.answer_text: Agility, lifelong learning, collaboration across silos and willingness to reskill
questions.explanation: Industry 4.0 demands agility, reskilling and cross-functional collaboration.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which duty BEST describes a digital leader?

options.a: Avoiding change so that operations remain stable during periods of uncertainty
options.b: Guiding the organisation through digital transformation and driving adoption of digital tools and innovation
options.c: Approving only financial reports before they are submitted to regulators
options.d: Maintaining servers and ensuring that the network is available to every department

questions.answer_text: Guiding the organisation through digital transformation and driving adoption of digital tools and innovation
questions.explanation: Digital leaders drive adoption, culture and strategy in a rapidly changing landscape.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which theory underpins digital leadership by inspiring, motivating and leading change?

options.a: Transactional leadership
options.b: Transformational leadership
options.c: Autocratic leadership
options.d: Laissez-faire leadership

questions.answer_text: Transformational leadership
questions.explanation: Transformational leaders inspire innovation and drive cultural change.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: How does transformational leadership differ from traditional command-and-control leadership in digital contexts?

options.a: It discourages employee contributions so that teams stay within defined tasks
options.b: It centralises all decisions at the top so that direction is unambiguous
options.c: It inspires, empowers and encourages innovation, rather than relying on directives and strict control
options.d: It avoids vision and focuses on rules so that employees follow standard procedures

questions.answer_text: It inspires, empowers and encourages innovation, rather than relying on directives and strict control
questions.explanation: Transformational leaders inspire and empower rather than command.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which skill is MOST important for a digital leader?

options.a: Avoiding change management so that teams are free to adopt tools as they wish
options.b: Understanding key technologies such as AI, cloud and blockchain well enough to make informed decisions
options.c: Technical coding ability only, so that the leader can write software personally
options.d: Ignoring technology trends so that strategic decisions rest on established practice

questions.answer_text: Understanding key technologies such as AI, cloud and blockchain well enough to make informed decisions
questions.explanation: Digital leaders need technological fluency and change management skills.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Industry 4.0 design principles include which of the following?

options.a: Isolation, manual operation and batch processing of production data at night
options.b: Centralisation, paper records and delayed reporting from the shop floor
options.c: Interoperability, virtualisation, real-time capability and service orientation
options.d: Rigidity, secrecy and sequential-only workflows that rely on manual sign-off

questions.answer_text: Interoperability, virtualisation, real-time capability and service orientation
questions.explanation: The design principles enable end-to-end digital integration of value chains.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which future technology pair will deepen connectivity and intelligence in Industry 4.0?

options.a: Manual ledgers and typewriters that record transactions and correspondence
options.b: Mainframes and punch cards that process large batches of data overnight
options.c: Telex and fax networks that exchange documents between regional offices
options.d: 5G and blockchain together with AI and machine learning

questions.answer_text: 5G and blockchain together with AI and machine learning
questions.explanation: The course highlights 5G, blockchain, AI and ML as future enablers.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Why is Industry 4.0 described as a paradigm shift rather than an evolution?

options.a: It does not change customer engagement, because production stays behind the scenes
options.b: It simply replaces older machines with faster ones, leaving business models unchanged
options.c: It only affects the marketing of the manufacturing sector's finished products
options.d: The fusion of IoT, AI, CPS and cloud transforms industries through smart products, servitisation and real-time analytics

questions.answer_text: The fusion of IoT, AI, CPS and cloud transforms industries through smart products, servitisation and real-time analytics
questions.explanation: Industry 4.0 changes business models and customer engagement, not just machinery.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Which statement about big data in Industry 4.0 is MOST accurate?

options.a: Machine and system data are analysed to optimise production, predict maintenance and improve supply chains
options.b: Data collected by sensors is unused because analysis occurs only at the end of the year
options.c: Big data is limited to marketing and has no role in production or supply chains
options.d: Big data replaces the need for IoT because analytics can run without any sensors

questions.answer_text: Machine and system data are analysed to optimise production, predict maintenance and improve supply chains
questions.explanation: Analytics turn machine data into actionable insights.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: Cloud computing in Industry 4.0 primarily provides:

options.a: Isolated local storage that keeps factory data separate from the supply chain
options.b: Printed manuals and training materials for operators on the shop floor
options.c: On-demand storage, servers and applications enabling data sharing and collaboration across supply chains
options.d: Physical production machinery that manufactures components in factory locations

questions.answer_text: On-demand storage, servers and applications enabling data sharing and collaboration across supply chains
questions.explanation: Cloud supports scalable, shared data infrastructure for connected operations.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: A firm adopts IoT sensors but lacks staff who can interpret data. Which challenge is this?

options.a: Excess data security that prevents staff from accessing the information they need
options.b: Too many customers for the factory to serve with existing production capacity
options.c: Over-regulation that forbids manufacturers from using connected sensors
options.d: Skills shortage, requiring training or hiring of specialised professionals

questions.answer_text: Skills shortage, requiring training or hiring of specialised professionals
questions.explanation: Organisations must invest in training or hire specialised talent.

questions.module_title: Industry 4.0, IoT, and Digital Leadership
questions.question: A leader breaks down silos and promotes collaboration among IT, operations and business teams. Which requirement of Industry 4.0 is being met?

options.a: Reduced communication so that each team concentrates on its own responsibilities
options.b: Avoidance of technology so that employees rely on established working methods
options.c: Leadership that fosters an open, cross-functional culture able to adapt to technological change
options.d: Rigid reporting lines so that decisions follow the traditional management hierarchy

questions.answer_text: Leadership that fosters an open, cross-functional culture able to adapt to technological change
questions.explanation: Industry 4.0 requires leaders to break down silos and build adaptive cultures.
